units.leftText: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
units.rightText: Adam, Seth, Enosh,

units.leftText: Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
units.rightText: Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,

units.leftText: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
units.rightText: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah.

units.leftText: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
units.rightText: The sons of Noah:
rightNotes: 1:4 LXX; Hebrew does not include The sons of Noah:; see Genesis 5:32|GEN 5:32*.

units.leftText: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
units.rightText: The sons of Japheth:

units.leftText: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
units.rightText: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
rightNotes: 1:6 Many Hebrew manuscripts and Vulgate (see also LXX and Genesis 10:3|GEN 10:3*); most Hebrew manuscripts Diphath

units.leftText: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
units.rightText: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.

units.leftText: The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
units.rightText: The sons of Ham:

units.leftText: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
units.rightText: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca.
rightNotes: 1:9 Sabta is a variant of Sabtah; see Genesis 10:7|GEN 10:7*.

units.leftText: Cush became the father of Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one on the earth.
units.rightText: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
rightNotes: 1:10 Or who established himself as a mighty warrior

units.leftText: Mizraim became the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
units.rightText: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

units.leftText: Pathrusim, Casluhim (where the Philistines came from), and Caphtorim.
units.rightText: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
rightNotes: 1:12 Some translators adjust the Hebrew word order to the Casluhites, and the Caphtorites (from whom the Philistines came); see also Jeremiah 47:4|JER 47:4* and Amos 9:7.

units.leftText: Canaan became the father of Sidon his firstborn, Heth,
units.rightText: And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
rightNotes: 1:13 Or of the Sidonians, the foremost
1:13 Hebrew and of Heth

units.leftText: the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,
units.rightText: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

units.leftText: the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,
units.rightText: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

units.leftText: the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
units.rightText: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.

units.leftText: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
units.rightText: The sons of Shem:

units.leftText: Arpachshad became the father of Shelah, and Shelah became the father of Eber.
units.rightText: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.

units.leftText: To Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
units.rightText: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
rightNotes: 1:19 Peleg means division.

units.leftText: Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
units.rightText: And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

units.leftText: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
units.rightText: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

units.leftText: Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
units.rightText: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
rightNotes: 1:22 LXX and Syriac (see also Genesis 10:28|GEN 10:28*); Hebrew Ebal

units.leftText: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
units.rightText: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

units.leftText: Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
units.rightText: So from Shem came Arphaxad, Shelah,
rightNotes: 1:24 Literally Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah; some LXX manuscripts Shem, Arphaxad, Cainan, Shelah; see also Genesis 10:24|GEN 10:24* LXX and Luke 3:35–36.

units.leftText: Eber, Peleg, Reu,
units.rightText: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

units.leftText: Serug, Nahor, Terah,
units.rightText: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

units.leftText: Abram (also called Abraham).
units.rightText: and Abram (that is, Abraham).

units.leftText: The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
units.rightText: The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishmael.

units.leftText: These are their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
units.rightText: These are their genealogies:

units.leftText: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
units.rightText: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,

units.leftText: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.
units.rightText: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.

units.leftText: The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
units.rightText: The sons born to Keturah, Abraham’s concubine:

units.leftText: The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
units.rightText: The sons of Midian:

units.leftText: Abraham became the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
units.rightText: Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac:

units.leftText: The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
units.rightText: The sons of Esau:

units.leftText: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
units.rightText: The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz; and by Timna, Amalek.
rightNotes: 1:36 Many Hebrew manuscripts, some LXX manuscripts, and Syriac (see also Genesis 36:11|GEN 36:11*); most Hebrew manuscripts Zephi

units.leftText: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
units.rightText: The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

units.leftText: The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
units.rightText: The sons of Seir:

units.leftText: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Timna was Lotan’s sister.
units.rightText: The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.
rightNotes: 1:39 Homam is a variant of Hemam; see Genesis 36:22|GEN 36:22*.

units.leftText: The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
units.rightText: The sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
rightNotes: 1:40 LXX (see also Genesis 36:23|GEN 36:23*); Hebrew Alian
1:40 LXX (see also Genesis 36:23|GEN 36:23*); Hebrew Shephi

units.leftText: The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
units.rightText: The son of Anah: Dishon.
rightNotes: 1:41 Hebrew sons

units.leftText: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
units.rightText: The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
rightNotes: 1:42 LXX (see also Genesis 36:27|GEN 36:27*); Hebrew Jaakan

units.leftText: Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel: Bela the son of Beor; and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
units.rightText: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites:
rightNotes: 1:43 Or before an Israelite king ruled over them

units.leftText: Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
units.rightText: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Avith.

units.leftText: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigned in his place.
rightNotes: 1:48 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Shaul died, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
units.rightText: When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Baal Hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Pai. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
units.rightText: When Baal-hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place. His city was named Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
rightNotes: 1:50 Many MT manuscripts, some LXX manuscripts, Vulgate, and Syriac (see also Genesis 36:39|GEN 36:39*); most MT manuscripts Pai

units.leftText: Then Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,
units.rightText: Then Hadad died.

units.leftText: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
units.rightText: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

units.leftText: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
units.rightText: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

units.leftText: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
units.rightText: Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
units.rightText: These were the sons of Israel:

units.leftText: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
units.rightText: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

units.leftText: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah, which three were born to him of Shua’s daughter the Canaanitess. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the LORD’s sight; and he killed him.
units.rightText: The sons of Judah:
leftNotes: 2:3 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.
units.rightText: Tamar, Judah’s daughter-in-law, bore to him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.

units.leftText: The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
units.rightText: The sons of Perez:

units.leftText: The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five of them in all.
units.rightText: The sons of Zerah:

units.leftText: The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who committed a trespass in the devoted thing.
units.rightText: The son of Carmi:
rightNotes: 2:7 Hebrew sons

units.leftText: The son of Ethan: Azariah.
units.rightText: The son of Ethan:

units.leftText: The sons also of Hezron, who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
units.rightText: The sons who were born to Hezron:

units.leftText: Ram became the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah;
units.rightText: Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, a leader of the descendants of Judah.

units.leftText: and Nahshon became the father of Salma, and Salma became the father of Boaz,
units.rightText: Nahshon was the father of Salmon, and Salmon was the father of Boaz.
rightNotes: 2:11 LXX (see also Ruth 4:20–21|RUT 4:20-21*); Hebrew Salma; twice in this verse

units.leftText: and Boaz became the father of Obed, and Obed became the father of Jesse;
units.rightText: Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.

units.leftText: and Jesse became the father of his firstborn Eliab, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,
units.rightText: Jesse was the father of Eliab his firstborn; Abinadab was born second, Shimea third,
rightNotes: 2:13 Shimea is a variant of Shammah, Shimeah, and Shimei; see 1 Samuel 16:9|1SA 16:9*, 2 Samuel 13:3, and 2 Samuel 21:21.

units.leftText: Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
units.rightText: Nethanel fourth, Raddai fifth,

units.leftText: Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh;
units.rightText: Ozem sixth, and David seventh.

units.leftText: and their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.
units.rightText: Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. And the three sons of Zeruiah were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.

units.leftText: Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
units.rightText: Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
rightNotes: 2:17 Jether is a variant of Ithra; see 2 Samuel 17:25|2SA 17:25*.

units.leftText: Caleb the son of Hezron became the father of children by Azubah his wife, and by Jerioth; and these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
units.rightText: Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth. These were the sons of Azubah: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

units.leftText: Azubah died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
units.rightText: When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore to him Hur.
rightNotes: 2:19 Ephrath is a variant of Ephrathah; see verse 50.

units.leftText: Hur became the father of Uri, and Uri became the father of Bezalel.
units.rightText: Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.

units.leftText: Afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he took as wife when he was sixty years old; and she bore him Segub.
units.rightText: Later, Hezron slept with the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead. He had married her when he was sixty years old, and she bore to him Segub.

units.leftText: Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
units.rightText: Segub was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

units.leftText: Geshur and Aram took the towns of Jair from them, with Kenath, and its villages, even sixty cities. All these were the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.
units.rightText: But Geshur and Aram captured Havvoth-jair, along with Kenath and its sixty surrounding villages. All these were descendants of Machir the father of Gilead.
rightNotes: 2:23 Or the villages of Jair

units.leftText: After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah, Hezron’s wife, bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
units.rightText: After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore to him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
rightNotes: 2:24 Or After Hezron died, Caleb had relations with Ephrathah, the wife of Hezron his father, and she bore; see also LXX.
2:24 Or the founder; also in verses 42, 45, 49, and possibly elsewhere

units.leftText: The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron were Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
units.rightText: The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron:

units.leftText: Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah. She was the mother of Onam.
units.rightText: Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah, who was the mother of Onam.

units.leftText: The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
units.rightText: The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel:

units.leftText: The sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
units.rightText: The sons of Onam:

units.leftText: The name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail; and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
units.rightText: Abishur’s wife was named Abihail, and she bore to him Ahban and Molid.

units.leftText: The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; but Seled died without children.
units.rightText: The sons of Nadab:

units.leftText: The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai.
units.rightText: The son of Appaim:
rightNotes: 2:31 Hebrew sons; three times in this verse

units.leftText: The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether died without children.
units.rightText: The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai:

units.leftText: The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.
units.rightText: The sons of Jonathan:

units.leftText: Now Sheshan had no sons, but only daughters. Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha.
units.rightText: Sheshan had no sons, but only daughters. He also had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.

units.leftText: Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as wife; and she bore him Attai.
units.rightText: Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore to him Attai.

units.leftText: Attai became the father of Nathan, and Nathan became the father of Zabad,
units.rightText: Attai was the father of Nathan, Nathan was the father of Zabad,

units.leftText: and Zabad became the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal became the father of Obed,
units.rightText: Zabad was the father of Ephlal, Ephlal was the father of Obed,

units.leftText: and Obed became the father of Jehu, and Jehu became the father of Azariah,
units.rightText: Obed was the father of Jehu, Jehu was the father of Azariah,

units.leftText: and Azariah became the father of Helez, and Helez became the father of Eleasah,
units.rightText: Azariah was the father of Helez, Helez was the father of Elasah,

units.leftText: and Eleasah became the father of Sismai, and Sismai became the father of Shallum,
units.rightText: Elasah was the father of Sismai, Sismai was the father of Shallum,

units.leftText: and Shallum became the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah became the father of Elishama.
units.rightText: Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.

units.leftText: The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
units.rightText: The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel:

units.leftText: The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
units.rightText: The sons of Hebron:

units.leftText: Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem became the father of Shammai.
units.rightText: Shema was the father of Raham the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem was the father of Shammai.

units.leftText: The son of Shammai was Maon; and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
units.rightText: The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.

units.leftText: Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; and Haran became the father of Gazez.
units.rightText: Caleb’s concubine Ephah was the mother of Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.

units.leftText: The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
units.rightText: The sons of Jahdai:

units.leftText: Maacah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
units.rightText: Caleb’s concubine Maacah was the mother of Sheber and Tirhanah.

units.leftText: She bore also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbena and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb was Achsah.
units.rightText: She was also the mother of Shaaph father of Madmannah, and of Sheva father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb’s daughter was Acsah.

units.leftText: These were the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim,
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Caleb.

units.leftText: Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader.
units.rightText: Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader.

units.leftText: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim:

units.leftText: The families of Kiriath Jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
units.rightText: and the clans of Kiriath-jearim— the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From these descended the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.

units.leftText: The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
units.rightText: The descendants of Salma:

units.leftText: The families of scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
units.rightText: and the clans of the scribes who lived at Jabez— the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
rightNotes: 2:55 Or of the Sopherites
2:55 Or the father of Beth-rekab or the founder of the house of Rechab

units.leftText: Now these were the sons of David, who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second, Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess;
units.rightText: These were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron:

units.leftText: the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith;
units.rightText: the third was Absalom the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur;

units.leftText: the fifth, Shephatiah of Abital; the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife:
units.rightText: the fifth was Shephatiah by Abital;

units.leftText: six were born to him in Hebron; and he reigned there seven years and six months. He reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem;
units.rightText: These six sons were born to David in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months.

units.leftText: and these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four, by Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel;
units.rightText: and these sons were born to him in Jerusalem:

units.leftText: and Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
units.rightText: David’s other sons were Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet,
rightNotes: 3:6 Hebrew does not include David’s other sons were.
3:6 Two Hebrew manuscripts (see also 2 Samuel 5:15|2SA 5:15* and 1 Chronicles 14:5); most Hebrew manuscripts Elishama

units.leftText: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
units.rightText: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

units.leftText: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine.
units.rightText: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet— nine in all.

units.leftText: All these were the sons of David, in addition to the sons of the concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
units.rightText: These were all the sons of David, besides the sons by his concubines. And Tamar was their sister.

units.leftText: Solomon’s son was Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
units.rightText: Solomon’s son was Rehoboam:

units.leftText: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
units.rightText: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
rightNotes: 3:11 Joram is a variant spelling of Jehoram.

units.leftText: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
units.rightText: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
rightNotes: 3:12 Azariah is also called Uzziah; see 2 Chronicles 26:1|2CH 26:1*.

units.leftText: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
units.rightText: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,

units.leftText: Amon his son, and Josiah his son.
units.rightText: Amon his son, and Josiah his son.

units.leftText: The sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum.
units.rightText: The sons of Josiah:

units.leftText: The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, and Zedekiah his son.
units.rightText: The successors of Jehoiakim:

units.leftText: The sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son,
units.rightText: The descendants of Jeconiah the captive:

units.leftText: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
units.rightText: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.

leftNotes: 4:9 “Jabez” sounds similar to the Hebrew word for “pain”.
rightNotes: 4:9 Jabez sounds like the Hebrew for pain or distress.

units.leftText: Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, “Oh that you would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border! May your hand be with me, and may you keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!”
units.rightText: And Jabez called out to the God of Israel, “If only You would bless me and enlarge my territory! May Your hand be with me and keep me from harm, so that I will be free from pain.”

units.leftText: They went to the entrance of Gedor, even to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
units.rightText: and they journeyed to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, in search of pasture for their flocks.

units.leftText: They found rich, good pasture, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceful, for those who lived there before were descended from Ham.
units.rightText: There they found rich, good pasture, and the land was spacious, peaceful, and quiet; for some Hamites had lived there formerly.

units.leftText: These written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck their tents and the Meunim who were found there; and they destroyed them utterly to this day, and lived in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
units.rightText: These who were noted by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites in their dwellings as well as the Meunites who were there, devoting them to destruction even to this day. Then they settled in their place, because there was pasture for their flocks.
rightNotes: 4:41 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: Some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
units.rightText: And five hundred of these Simeonites led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, went to Mount Seir

units.leftText: They struck the remnant of the Amalekites who escaped, and have lived there to this day.
units.rightText: and struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped. And they have lived there to this day.

units.leftText: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel (for he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph the son of Israel; and the genealogy is not to be listed according to the birthright.
units.rightText: These were the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel. Though he was the firstborn, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, because Reuben defiled his father’s bed. So he is not reckoned according to birthright.

units.leftText: For Judah prevailed above his brothers, and from him came the prince; but the birthright was Joseph’s)—
units.rightText: And though Judah prevailed over his brothers and a ruler came from him, the birthright belonged to Joseph.

units.leftText: and he lived eastward even to the entrance of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, because their livestock were multiplied in the land of Gilead.
units.rightText: They also settled in the east as far as the edge of the desert that extends to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead.

units.leftText: In the days of Saul, they made war with the Hagrites, who fell by their hand; and they lived in their tents throughout all the land east of Gilead.
units.rightText: During the days of Saul they waged war against the Hagrites, who were defeated at their hands, and they occupied the dwellings of the Hagrites throughout the region east of Gilead.

units.leftText: The sons of Gad lived beside them in the land of Bashan to Salecah:
units.rightText: The descendants of Gad lived next to the Reubenites in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah:

units.leftText: Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
units.rightText: Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Jaanai and Shaphat, who lived in Bashan.

units.leftText: Their brothers of their fathers’ houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven.
units.rightText: Their kinsmen by families were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber— seven in all.

units.rightText: These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.

units.rightText: Ahi son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was head of their family.

units.rightText: They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon.

units.leftText: All these were listed by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
units.rightText: All of them were recorded in the genealogies during the reigns of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.

units.leftText: The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, able to shoot with bow, and skillful in war, were forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty that were able to go out to war.
units.rightText: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 warriors— valiant men who carried the shield and sword, drew the bow, and were trained for battle.

units.leftText: They made war with the Hagrites, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
units.rightText: They waged war against the Hagrites, as well as Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

units.leftText: They were helped against them, and the Hagrites were delivered into their hand, and all who were with them; for they cried to God in the battle, and he answered them because they put their trust in him.
units.rightText: And because they cried out to God in battle, they were helped against their enemies, and the Hagrites and all their allies were delivered into their hands. Because they put their trust in God, He answered their prayers.

units.leftText: They took away their livestock: of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred fifty thousand, and of donkeys two thousand, and of men one hundred thousand.
units.rightText: They seized the livestock of the Hagrites— 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 captives,

units.leftText: For many fell slain, because the war was of God. They lived in their place until the captivity.
units.rightText: and many others fell slain, because the battle belonged to God. And they occupied the land until the exile.

units.leftText: The children of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They increased from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
units.rightText: Now the people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were numerous. They settled in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon (that is, Senir, also known as Mount Hermon).
rightNotes: 5:23 Literally from Bashan to Baal-hermon and Senir and Mount Hermon.

units.leftText: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: These were the heads of their families:

units.leftText: They trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the prostitute after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God destroyed before them.
units.rightText: But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves with the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

units.leftText: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the river of Gozan, to this day.
units.rightText: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria) to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. And he brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.

units.leftText: the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
units.rightText: the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.

units.leftText: On the left hand their brothers the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
units.rightText: On the left were their kinsmen, the sons of Merari:

units.leftText: the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
units.rightText: the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,

units.leftText: the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
units.rightText: the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,

units.leftText: the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
units.rightText: the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.

units.leftText: Their brothers the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of God’s house.
units.rightText: Their fellow Levites were assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God.

units.leftText: But Aaron and his sons offered on the altar of burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
units.rightText: But Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place. They presented the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
rightNotes: 6:49 Or the Holy of Holies

units.leftText: These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Aaron:

units.leftText: Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
units.rightText: Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,

units.leftText: Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
units.rightText: Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,

units.leftText: Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
units.rightText: Zadok his son, and Ahimaaz his son.

units.leftText: Now these are their dwelling places according to their encampments in their borders: to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites (for theirs was the first lot),
units.rightText: Now these were the territories assigned to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clan for their settlements, because the first lot fell to them:

units.leftText: to them they gave Hebron in the land of Judah, and its pasture lands around it;
units.rightText: They were given Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands.

units.leftText: but the fields of the city and its villages, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
units.rightText: But the fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.

units.leftText: To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge, Hebron, Libnah also with its pasture lands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: So the descendants of Aaron were given Hebron (a city of refuge), Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa,
rightNotes: 6:57 As in the parallel text at Joshua 21:13|JOS 21:13*; Hebrew were given the cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah

units.leftText: Hilen with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: Hilen, Debir,
rightNotes: 6:58 Some Hebrew manuscripts; MT Hilez; parallel text at Joshua 21:15|JOS 21:15* Holon

units.leftText: Ashan with its pasture lands, and Beth Shemesh with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: Ashan, Juttah, and Beth-shemesh, together with their pasturelands.
rightNotes: 6:59 Ashan is a variant of Ain; see Joshua 21:16|JOS 21:16*.
6:59 Syriac and the parallel text at Joshua 21:16|JOS 21:16*; MT does not include Juttah,

units.leftText: and out of the tribe of Benjamin, Geba with its pasture lands, Allemeth with its pasture lands, and Anathoth with its pasture lands. All their cities throughout their families were thirteen cities.
units.rightText: And from the tribe of Benjamin they were given Gibeon, Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, together with their pasturelands. So they had thirteen cities in all among their families.
rightNotes: 6:60 LXX, Syriac, and parallel text at Joshua 21:17|JOS 21:17*; MT does not include Gibeon,

units.leftText: To the rest of the sons of Kohath were given by lot, out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.
units.rightText: To the rest of the Kohathites, ten cities were allotted from the half-tribe of Manasseh.

units.leftText: To the sons of Gershom, according to their families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
units.rightText: The Gershomites , according to their clans, were allotted thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan.
rightNotes: 6:62 Gershomites is a variant of Gershonites; also in verse 71; see 1 Chronicles 23:7|1CH 23:7*.

units.leftText: To the sons of Merari were given by lot, according to their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities.
units.rightText: The Merarites, according to their clans, were allotted twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

units.leftText: The children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities with their pasture lands.
units.rightText: So the Israelites gave to the Levites these cities and their pasturelands.

units.leftText: They gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities which are mentioned by name.
units.rightText: They assigned by lot the cities named above from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.

units.leftText: Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim.
units.rightText: And some of the clans of the Kohathites were given cities from the tribe of Ephraim for their territory:

units.leftText: They gave to them the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim with its pasture lands and Gezer with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: They were given Shechem (a city of refuge) with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer,
rightNotes: 6:67 As in the parallel text at Joshua 21:21|JOS 21:21*; Hebrew They were given the cities of refuge: Shechem

units.leftText: Jokmeam with its pasture lands, Beth Horon with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: Jokmeam, Beth-horon,

units.leftText: Aijalon with its pasture lands, Gath Rimmon with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: Aijalon, and Gath-rimmon, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner with its pasture lands, and Bileam with its pasture lands, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath.
units.rightText: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh the rest of the clans of the Kohathites were given Aner and Bileam, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: To the sons of Gershom were given, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its pasture lands, and Ashtaroth with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: The Gershomites received the following:

units.leftText: and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: From the tribe of Issachar they were given Kedesh, Daberath,

units.leftText: Ramoth with its pasture lands, and Anem with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: Ramoth, and Anem, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: and out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: From the tribe of Asher they were given Mashal, Abdon,

units.leftText: Hukok with its pasture lands, and Rehob with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: Hukok, and Rehob, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, Hammon with its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim with its pasture lands.
units.rightText: And from the tribe of Naphtali they were given Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: To the rest of the Levites, the sons of Merari, were given, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono with its pasture lands, and Tabor with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: The Merarites (the rest of the Levites) received the following:

units.leftText: and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, were given them out of the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness with its pasture lands, Jahzah with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: From the tribe of Reuben east of the Jordan opposite Jericho they were given Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah,
rightNotes: 6:78 Jahzah is a variant of Jahaz; see Numbers 21:23|NUM 21:23*.

units.leftText: Kedemoth with its pasture lands, and Mephaath with its pasture lands;
units.rightText: Kedemoth, and Mephaath, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
units.rightText: And from the tribe of Gad they were given Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,

units.leftText: Heshbon with its pasture lands, and Jazer with its pasture lands.
units.rightText: Heshbon, and Jazer, together with their pasturelands.

units.leftText: Of the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.
units.rightText: The sons of Issachar:

units.leftText: The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their fathers’ houses, of Tola; mighty men of valor in their generations. Their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: The sons of Tola:

units.leftText: The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five; all of them chief men.
units.rightText: The son of Uzzi:
rightNotes: 7:3 Hebrew sons; also in verses 10 and 17

units.leftText: With them, by their generations, after their fathers’ houses, were bands of the army for war, thirty-six thousand; for they had many wives and sons.
units.rightText: In addition to them, according to their genealogy, they had 36,000 troops for battle, for they had many wives and children.

units.leftText: Their brothers among all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, listed in all by genealogy, were eighty-seven thousand.
units.rightText: Their kinsmen belonging to all the families of Issachar who were mighty men of valor totaled 87,000, as listed in their genealogies.

units.leftText: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three.
units.rightText: The three sons of Benjamin:

units.leftText: The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor; and they were listed by genealogy twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
units.rightText: The sons of Bela:

units.leftText: The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.
units.rightText: The sons of Becher:

units.leftText: They were listed by genealogy, after their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor, twenty thousand two hundred.
units.rightText: Their genealogies were recorded according to the heads of their families— 20,200 mighty men of valor.

units.leftText: The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
units.rightText: The son of Jediael:

units.leftText: All these were sons of Jediael, according to the heads of their fathers’ households, mighty men of valor, seventeen thousand two hundred, who were able to go out in the army for war.
units.rightText: All these sons of Jediael were heads of their families, mighty men of valor; there were 17,200 fit for battle.

units.leftText: So were Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, and the sons of Aher.
units.rightText: The Shuppites and Huppites were descendants of Ir, and the Hushites were descendants of Aher.

units.leftText: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum, and the sons of Bilhah.
units.rightText: The sons of Naphtali:

units.leftText: The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bore. She bore Machir the father of Gilead.
units.rightText: The descendants of Manasseh: Asriel

units.leftText: Machir took a wife of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister’s name was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters.
units.rightText: Machir took a wife from among the Huppites and Shuppites. The name of his sister was Maacah.

units.leftText: Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she named him Peresh. The name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
units.rightText: Machir’s wife Maacah gave birth to a son, and she named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.

units.leftText: The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
units.rightText: The son of Ulam:

units.leftText: His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
units.rightText: His sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

units.leftText: The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
units.rightText: And these were the sons of Shemida:

units.leftText: The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
units.rightText: The descendants of Ephraim:

units.leftText: Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because they came down to take away their livestock.
units.rightText: Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son.

units.leftText: Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
units.rightText: Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his relatives came to comfort him.

units.leftText: He went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Beriah, because there was trouble with his house.
units.rightText: And again he slept with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. So he named him Beriah, because tragedy had come upon his house.
leftNotes: 7:23 “Beriah” is similar to the Hebrew word for “misfortune”.
rightNotes: 7:23 Beriah sounds like the Hebrew for tragedy or disaster.

units.leftText: His daughter was Sheerah, who built Beth Horon the lower and the upper, and Uzzen Sheerah.
units.rightText: His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, as well as Uzzen-sheerah.

units.leftText: Rephah was his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
units.rightText: Additionally, Rephah was his son, Resheph his son, Telah his son, Tahan his son,
rightNotes: 7:25 Some LXX manuscripts; Hebrew does not include his son.

units.leftText: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
units.rightText: Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

units.leftText: Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
units.rightText: Nun his son, and Joshua his son.
rightNotes: 7:27 Or Non

units.leftText: Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;
units.rightText: Their holdings and settlements included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages as far as Ayyah and its villages.
rightNotes: 7:28 Ayyah is another name for Gaza; see also LXX.

units.leftText: and by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth Shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, and Dor and its towns. The children of Joseph the son of Israel lived in these.
units.rightText: And along the borders of Manasseh were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, together with their villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these towns.
rightNotes: 7:29 Beth-shean is a variant of Beth-shan; see 1 Samuel 31:10|1SA 31:10* and 2 Samuel 21:12.

units.leftText: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was their sister.
units.rightText: The children of Asher:

units.leftText: The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
units.rightText: The sons of Beriah:

units.leftText: Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
units.rightText: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and of their sister Shua.

units.leftText: The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet.
units.rightText: The sons of Japhlet:

units.leftText: The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
units.rightText: The sons of Shemer:

units.leftText: The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
units.rightText: The sons of his brother Helem:
rightNotes: 7:35 Helem is possibly another name for Hotham; see verse 32.

units.leftText: The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
units.rightText: The sons of Zophah:

units.leftText: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
units.rightText: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
rightNotes: 7:37 Ithran is possibly a variant of Jether; see verse 38.

units.leftText: The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
units.rightText: The sons of Jether:

units.leftText: The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
units.rightText: The sons of Ulla:

units.leftText: All these were the children of Asher, heads of the fathers’ houses, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes. The number of them listed by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.
units.rightText: All these were the descendants of Asher — heads of their families, choice and mighty men of valor, and chiefs among the leaders. The number of men fit for battle, recorded in their genealogies, was 26,000.

units.leftText: Benjamin became the father of Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,
units.rightText: Benjamin was the father of Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,

units.leftText: Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
units.rightText: Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.

units.leftText: Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
units.rightText: The sons of Bela:

units.leftText: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
units.rightText: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,

units.leftText: Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
units.rightText: Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Ehud. These are the heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Geba, who were carried captive to Manahath:
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Ehud who were the heads of the families living in Geba and were exiled to Manahath:

units.leftText: Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who carried them captive; and he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
units.rightText: Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who carried them into exile and who was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
rightNotes: 8:7 Or and Gera, that is Heglam, who was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.

units.leftText: Shaharaim became the father of children in the field of Moab, after he had sent them away. Hushim and Baara were his wives.
units.rightText: Shaharaim had sons in the country of Moab after he had divorced his wives Hushim and Baara.

units.leftText: By Hodesh his wife, he became the father of Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
units.rightText: His sons by his wife Hodesh:

units.leftText: Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of fathers’ households.
units.rightText: Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of families.

units.leftText: By Hushim, he became the father of Abitub and Elpaal.
units.rightText: He also had sons by Hushim:

units.leftText: The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod, with its towns;
units.rightText: The sons of Elpaal:

units.leftText: and Beriah and Shema, who were heads of fathers’ households of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gath;
units.rightText: and Beriah and Shema (who were the heads of families living in Aijalon and who drove out the inhabitants of Gath).

units.leftText: and Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
units.rightText: Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,

units.leftText: Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
units.rightText: Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,

units.leftText: Michael, Ishpah, Joha, the sons of Beriah,
units.rightText: Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were the sons of Beriah.

units.leftText: Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
units.rightText: Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,

units.leftText: Ishmerai, Izliah, Jobab, the sons of Elpaal,
units.rightText: Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal.

units.leftText: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
units.rightText: Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,

units.leftText: Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
units.rightText: Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,

units.leftText: Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath, the sons of Shimei,
units.rightText: Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei.

units.leftText: Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
units.rightText: Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,

units.leftText: Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
units.rightText: Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,

units.leftText: Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
units.rightText: Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,

units.leftText: Iphdeiah, Penuel, the sons of Shashak,
units.rightText: Iphdeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.

units.leftText: Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
units.rightText: Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,

units.leftText: Jaareshiah, Elijah, Zichri, and the sons of Jeroham.
units.rightText: Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham.

units.leftText: These were heads of fathers’ households throughout their generations, chief men. These lived in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: All these were heads of families, the chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: The father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon
units.rightText: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah,
rightNotes: 8:29 Some LXX manuscripts (see also 1 Chronicles 9:35|1CH 9:35*); Hebrew The father of Gibeon lived

units.leftText: with his firstborn son Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
units.rightText: and Abdon was his firstborn son, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
rightNotes: 8:30 Some LXX manuscripts include Ner; see 1 Chronicles 9:36|1CH 9:36*.

units.leftText: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
units.rightText: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
rightNotes: 8:31 Zecher is likely a variant of Zechariah; see 1 Chronicles 9:37|1CH 9:37*.

units.leftText: and Mikloth, who became the father of Shimeah. They also lived with their families in Jerusalem, near their relatives.
units.rightText: and Mikloth, who was the father of Shimeah. They too lived alongside their relatives in Jerusalem.
rightNotes: 8:32 Shimeah is a variant of Shimeam; see 1 Chronicles 9:38|1CH 9:38*.

units.leftText: Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
units.rightText: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
rightNotes: 8:33 Esh-baal is also called Ish-bosheth; see 2 Samuel 2:8|2SA 2:8*.

units.leftText: The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
units.rightText: The son of Jonathan:

units.leftText: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
units.rightText: The sons of Micah:

units.leftText: Ahaz became the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri became the father of Moza.
units.rightText: Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah, Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri was the father of Moza.
rightNotes: 8:36 Jehoaddah is a variant of Jarah or Jadah; see 1 Chronicles 9:42|1CH 9:42*.

units.leftText: Moza became the father of Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
units.rightText: Moza was the father of Binea. Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
rightNotes: 8:37 Raphah is a variant of Rephaiah; see 1 Chronicles 9:43|1CH 9:43*.

units.leftText: Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.
units.rightText: Azel had six sons, and these were their names:

units.leftText: The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
units.rightText: The sons of his brother Eshek:

units.leftText: The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons, and grandsons, one hundred fifty. All these were of the sons of Benjamin.
units.rightText: The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and they had many sons and grandsons— 150 in all.

units.leftText: So all Israel were listed by genealogies; and behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was carried away captive to Babylon for their disobedience.
units.rightText: So all Israel was recorded in the genealogies written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. But Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.
leftNotes: 9:1 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Now the first inhabitants who lived in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
units.rightText: Now the first to resettle their own property in their cities were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
rightNotes: 9:2 Hebrew Nethinim

units.leftText: In Jerusalem, there lived of the children of Judah, of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh:
units.rightText: Some of the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem:

units.leftText: Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Perez the son of Judah.
units.rightText: Uthai son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.

units.rightText: From the Shilonites:

units.leftText: Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their brothers, six hundred ninety.
units.rightText: From the Zerahites:

units.leftText: Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah;
units.rightText: From the Benjamites:

units.leftText: and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri; and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
units.rightText: Ibneiah son of Jeroham;

units.leftText: and their brothers, according to their generations, nine hundred fifty-six. All these men were heads of fathers’ households by their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: and 956 of their relatives according to their genealogy. All these men were heads of their families.

units.rightText: From the priests:

units.rightText: Azariah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief official of God’s temple;

units.rightText: Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah;

units.rightText: and 1,760 of their relatives, the heads of their families, able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

units.rightText: From the Levites:

units.rightText: Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph;

units.leftText: and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
units.rightText: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun;

units.leftText: The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers (Shallum was the chief),
units.rightText: These were the gatekeepers:

units.leftText: who previously served in the king’s gate eastward. They were the gatekeepers for the camp of the children of Levi.
units.rightText: he was previously stationed at the King’s Gate on the east side. These were the gatekeepers from the camp of the Levites.

units.leftText: Shallum was the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brothers, of his father’s house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent. Their fathers had been over the LORD’s camp, keepers of the entry.
units.rightText: Shallum son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his relatives from the Korahites were assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent, just as their fathers had been assigned to guard the entrance to the dwelling of the LORD.
rightNotes: 9:19 Ebiasaph is a variant of Abiasaph; see Exodus 6:24|EXO 6:24*.

units.leftText: Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past, and the LORD was with him.
units.rightText: In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him.

units.leftText: Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper of the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

units.leftText: All these who were chosen to be gatekeepers in the thresholds were two hundred twelve. These were listed by genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer ordained in their office of trust.
units.rightText: The number of those chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds was 212. They were registered by genealogy in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their positions of trust.

units.leftText: So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the LORD’s house, even the house of the tent, as guards.
units.rightText: So they and their descendants were assigned to guard the gates of the house of the LORD — the house called the Tent.

units.leftText: On the four sides were the gatekeepers, toward the east, west, north, and south.
units.rightText: The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south.

units.leftText: Their brothers, in their villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with them,
units.rightText: Their relatives came from their villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven-day periods.

units.leftText: for the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the rooms and over the treasuries in God’s house.
units.rightText: But the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God.

units.leftText: They stayed around God’s house, because that was their duty; and it was their duty to open it morning by morning.
units.rightText: They would spend the night stationed around the house of God, because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning.

units.leftText: Certain of them were in charge of the vessels of service, for these were brought in by count, and these were taken out by count.
units.rightText: Some of them were in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out.

units.leftText: Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
units.rightText: Others were put in charge of the furnishings and other articles of the sanctuary, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.

units.leftText: Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixing of the spices.
units.rightText: And some of the sons of the priests mixed the spices.

units.leftText: Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
units.rightText: A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the bread.

units.leftText: Some of their brothers, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the show bread, to prepare it every Sabbath.
units.rightText: Some of their Kohathite relatives were responsible for preparing the rows of the showbread every Sabbath.

units.leftText: These are the singers, heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, who lived in the rooms and were free from other service, for they were employed in their work day and night.
units.rightText: Those who were musicians, the heads of Levite families, stayed in the temple chambers and were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night.

units.leftText: These were heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men. They lived at Jerusalem.
units.rightText: All these were heads of Levite families, chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Jeiel the father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon.
units.rightText: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah.
rightNotes: 9:35 Or the founder

units.leftText: His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
units.rightText: Abdon was his firstborn son, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

units.leftText: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
units.rightText: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

units.leftText: Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They also lived with their relatives in Jerusalem, near their relatives.
units.rightText: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived alongside their relatives in Jerusalem.
rightNotes: 9:38 Shimeam is a variant of Shimeah; see 1 Chronicles 8:32|1CH 8:32*.

units.leftText: Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
units.rightText: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.

units.leftText: The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
units.rightText: The son of Jonathan:

units.rightText: The sons of Micah:

units.leftText: Moza became the father of Binea, Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
units.rightText: Moza was the father of Binea. Rephaiah was his son, Elasah his son, and Azel his son.

units.leftText: Azel had six sons, whose names are Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain on Mount Gilboa.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

units.leftText: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and after his sons; and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
units.rightText: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.

units.leftText: The battle went hard against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.
units.rightText: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his armor bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.”
units.rightText: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised men will come and torture me!”

units.leftText: When his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on his sword and died.
units.rightText: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died.

units.leftText: So Saul died with his three sons; and all his house died together.
units.rightText: So Saul died together with his three sons and all his house.

units.leftText: When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and lived in them.
units.rightText: When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.

units.leftText: On the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
units.rightText: The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

units.leftText: They stripped him and took his head and his armor, then sent into the land of the Philistines all around to carry the news to their idols and to the people.
units.rightText: They stripped Saul, cut off his head, took his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among their people.

units.leftText: They put his armor in the house of their gods, and fastened his head in the house of Dagon.
units.rightText: They put his armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of Dagon.

units.leftText: When all Jabesh Gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,
units.rightText: When all the people of Jabesh-gilead heard about everything the Philistines had done to Saul,

units.leftText: all the valiant men arose and took away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
units.rightText: all their men of valor set out and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons and brought them to Jabesh. And they buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.
rightNotes: 10:12 Or terebinth or great tree

units.leftText: So Saul died for his trespass which he committed against the LORD, because of the LORD’s word, which he didn’t keep, and also because he asked counsel of one who had a familiar spirit, to inquire,
units.rightText: So Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD, because he did not keep the word of the LORD and even consulted a medium for guidance,

units.leftText: and didn’t inquire of the LORD. Therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.
units.rightText: and he failed to inquire of the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.

units.leftText: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David to Hebron, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
units.rightText: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.

units.leftText: In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. The LORD your God said to you, ‘You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and you shall be prince over my people Israel.’”
units.rightText: Even in times past, while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. And the LORD your God said, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them.’”
rightNotes: 11:2 Or For some time

units.leftText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD. They anointed David king over Israel, according to the LORD’s word by Samuel.
units.rightText: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, where David made a covenant with them before the LORD. And they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel.

units.leftText: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem (also called Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.
units.rightText: Then David and all the Israelites marched to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus), where the Jebusites inhabited the land.

units.leftText: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here!” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city.
units.rightText: The people of Jebus said to David, “You will never get in here.”

units.leftText: David had said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and was made chief.
units.rightText: Now David had said, “Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander.”

units.leftText: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it David’s city.
units.rightText: So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David.

units.leftText: He built the city all around, from Millo even around; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
units.rightText: He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city.
rightNotes: 11:8 Hebrew the Millo

units.leftText: David grew greater and greater, for the LORD of Armies was with him.
units.rightText: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him.

units.leftText: Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the LORD’s word concerning Israel.
units.rightText: Now these were the chiefs of David’s mighty men, who, together with all Israel, bolstered and strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

units.leftText: This is the number of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them at one time.
units.rightText: This is the list of David’s mighty men:

units.leftText: After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men.
units.rightText: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
rightNotes: 11:12 Dodo is a variant of Dodai; see 1 Chronicles 27:4|1CH 27:4*.

units.leftText: He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where there was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.
units.rightText: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. At a place with a field full of barley, the troops fled from the Philistines.

units.leftText: They stood in the middle of the plot, defended it, and killed the Philistines; and the LORD saved them by a great victory.
units.rightText: But Eleazar and David stationed themselves in the middle of the field and defended it. They struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory.
rightNotes: 11:14 Literally But they stationed themselves

units.leftText: Three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: Three of the thirty chief men went down to David, to the rock at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem at that time.
units.rightText: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.

units.leftText: David longed, and said, “Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”
units.rightText: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”

units.leftText: The three broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, took it, and brought it to David; but David would not drink any of it, but poured it out to the LORD,
units.rightText: So the Three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead , he poured it out to the LORD,

units.leftText: and said, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?” For they risked their lives to bring it. Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.
units.rightText: saying, “Far be it from me, my God, to do this! How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?” Because they had brought it at the risk of their lives, David refused to drink it.

units.leftText: Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them, and had a name among the three.
units.rightText: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
rightNotes: 11:20 Hebrew; Syriac the Thirty; also in verse 21

units.leftText: Of the three, he was more honorable than the two, and was made their captain; however he wasn’t included in the three.
units.rightText: He was doubly honored above the Three, and he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.

units.leftText: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done mighty deeds, killed the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also went down and killed a lion in the middle of a pit on a snowy day.
units.rightText: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
rightNotes: 11:22 Or two sons of Ariel of Moab

units.leftText: He killed an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high. In the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
units.rightText: He also struck down an Egyptian, a huge man five cubits tall. Although the Egyptian had a spear like a weaver’s beam in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
leftNotes: 11:23 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. Therefore this Egyptian was about 7 feet and 6 inches or 2.28 meters tall.
rightNotes: 11:23 5 cubits is approximately 7 feet 6 inches or 229 centimeters tall.

units.leftText: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did these things and had a name among the three mighty men.
units.rightText: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name along with the three mighty men.

units.leftText: Behold, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three; and David set him over his guard.
units.rightText: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
