units.leftText: Some Gadites joined David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear; whose faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as the gazelles on the mountains:
units.rightText: Some Gadites defected to David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were mighty men of valor, trained for battle, experts with the shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:

units.leftText: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
units.rightText: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second in command, Eliab the third,

units.leftText: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
units.rightText: Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

units.leftText: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
units.rightText: Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

units.leftText: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
units.rightText: Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,

units.leftText: Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbannai the eleventh.
units.rightText: Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbanai the eleventh.

units.leftText: These of the sons of Gad were captains of the army. He who was least was equal to one hundred, and the greatest to one thousand.
units.rightText: These Gadites were army commanders, the least of whom was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.

units.leftText: These are those who went over the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all who lived in the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
units.rightText: These are the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month when it was overflowing all its banks, and they put to flight all those in the valleys, both to the east and to the west.

units.leftText: Some of the children of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.
units.rightText: Other Benjamites and some men from Judah also came to David in his stronghold.

units.leftText: David went out to meet them, and answered them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see this and rebuke it.”
units.rightText: And David went out to meet them, saying, “If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my enemies when my hands are free of violence, may the God of our fathers see it and judge you.”

units.leftText: Then the Spirit came on Amasai, who was chief of the thirty, and he said, “We are yours, David, and on your side, you son of Jesse. Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to your helpers; for your God helps you.” Then David received them and made them captains of the band.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he said:

units.leftText: Some of Manasseh also joined David when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle, but they didn’t help them, for the lords of the Philistines sent him away after consultation, saying, “He will desert to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.”
units.rightText: Some from Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. (They did not help the Philistines because the Philistine rulers consulted and sent David away, saying, “It will cost us our heads if he defects to his master Saul.”)

units.leftText: As he went to Ziklag, some from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who were of Manasseh.
units.rightText: When David went to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh defected to him:

units.leftText: They helped David against the band of raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor and were captains in the army.
units.rightText: They helped David against the raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor and commanders in the army.

units.leftText: For from day to day men came to David to help him, until there was a great army, like God’s army.
units.rightText: For at that time men came to David day after day to help him, until he had a great army, like the army of God.

units.leftText: These are the numbers of the heads of those who were armed for war, who came to David to Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the LORD’s word.
units.rightText: Now these are the numbers of men armed for battle who came to David at Hebron to turn Saul’s kingdom over to him, in accordance with the word of the LORD:

units.leftText: The children of Judah who bore shield and spear were six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.
units.rightText: From Judah: 6,800 armed troops bearing shields and spears.

units.leftText: Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war: seven thousand one hundred.
units.rightText: From Simeon: 7,100 mighty men of valor, ready for battle.

units.leftText: Of the children of Levi: four thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: From Levi: 4,600,

units.leftText: Jehoiada was the leader of the household of Aaron; and with him were three thousand seven hundred,
units.rightText: including Jehoiada, leader of the house of Aaron, with 3,700 men,

units.leftText: and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house twenty-two captains.
units.rightText: and Zadok, a mighty young man of valor, with 22 commanders from his own family.

units.leftText: Of the children of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives: three thousand, for until then, the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to Saul’s house.
units.rightText: From Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul: 3,000, most of whom had remained loyal to the house of Saul up to that time.

units.leftText: Of the children of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: From Ephraim: 20,800 mighty men of valor, famous among their own clans.

units.leftText: Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who were mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
units.rightText: From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 designated by name to come and make David king.
rightNotes: 12:31 That is, the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan

units.leftText: Of the children of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their heads were two hundred; and all their brothers were at their command.
units.rightText: From Issachar, men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: 200 chiefs with all their kinsmen at their command.

units.leftText: Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array with all kinds of instruments of war: fifty thousand who could command and were not of double heart.
units.rightText: From Zebulun: 50,000 fit for service, trained for battle with all kinds of weapons of war, who with one purpose were devoted to David.
rightNotes: 12:33 LXX; Hebrew does not include to David.

units.leftText: Of Naphtali: one thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty-seven thousand.
units.rightText: From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, accompanied by 37,000 men with shield and spear.

units.leftText: Of the Danites who could set the battle in array: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
units.rightText: From Dan: 28,600 prepared for battle.

units.leftText: Of Asher, such as were able to go out in the army, who could set the battle in array: forty thousand.
units.rightText: From Asher: 40,000 fit for service, prepared for battle.

units.leftText: On the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all kinds of instruments of war for the battle: one hundred twenty thousand.
units.rightText: And from east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh there: 120,000 armed with every kind of weapon of war.

units.leftText: All these were men of war who could order the battle array, and came with a perfect heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
units.rightText: All these men of war, arrayed for battle, came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of the Israelites were of one mind to make David king.

units.leftText: They were there with David three days, eating and drinking; for their brothers had supplied provisions for them.
units.rightText: They spent three days there eating and drinking with David, for their relatives had provided for them.

units.leftText: Moreover those who were near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought bread on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: supplies of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.
units.rightText: And their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali came bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen— abundant supplies of flour, fig cakes and raisin cakes, wine and oil, oxen and sheep. Indeed, there was joy in Israel.

units.leftText: David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader.
units.rightText: Then David conferred with all his leaders, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.

units.leftText: David said to all the assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of the LORD our God, let’s send word everywhere to our brothers who are left in all the land of Israel, with whom the priests and Levites are in their cities that have pasture lands, that they may gather themselves to us.
units.rightText: And he said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if this is of the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to the rest of our brothers in all the land of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, so that they may join us.

units.leftText: Also, let’s bring the ark of our God back to us again, for we didn’t seek it in the days of Saul.”
units.rightText: Then let us bring back the ark of our God, for we did not inquire of Him in the days of Saul.”
rightNotes: 13:3 Or of it

units.leftText: All the assembly said that they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
units.rightText: And because this proposal seemed right to all the people, the whole assembly agreed to it.

units.leftText: So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor River of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath Jearim.
units.rightText: So David assembled all Israel, from the River Shihor in Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.
rightNotes: 13:5 Hebrew from the Shihor

units.leftText: David went up with all Israel to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath Jearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up from there God the LORD’s ark that sits above the cherubim, that is called by the Name.
units.rightText: David and all Israel went up to Baalah of Judah (that is, Kiriath-jearim) to bring up from there the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim — the ark that is called by the Name.
rightNotes: 13:6 Or the ark of God, which is called by the Name of the LORD who is enthroned between the cherubim; or the ark of God, the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim, where His Name is called

units.leftText: They carried God’s ark on a new cart, and brought it out of Abinadab’s house; and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
units.rightText: So they carried the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding the cart.

units.leftText: David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
units.rightText: David and all the Israelites were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs and on harps and lyres, with tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

units.leftText: When they came to Chidon’s threshing floor, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
units.rightText: When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.
rightNotes: 13:9 Chidon is a variant of Nacon; see 2 Samuel 6:6|2SA 6:6*.

units.leftText: The LORD’s anger burned against Uzza, and he struck him because he put his hand on the ark; and he died there before God.
units.rightText: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and He struck him down because he had put his hand on the ark. So he died there before God.

units.leftText: David was displeased, because the LORD had broken out against Uzza. He called that place Perez Uzza, to this day.
units.rightText: Then David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.
rightNotes: 13:11 Perez-uzzah means outbreak against Uzzah.

units.leftText: David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring God’s ark home to me?”
units.rightText: That day David feared God and asked, “How can I ever bring the ark of God to me?”

units.leftText: So David didn’t move the ark with him into David’s city, but carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
units.rightText: So he did not move the ark with him to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

units.leftText: God’s ark remained with the family of Obed-Edom in his house three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-Edom’s house and all that he had.
units.rightText: Thus the ark of God remained with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his household and everything he owned.

units.leftText: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
units.rightText: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, stonemasons, and carpenters, to build a palace for him.

units.leftText: David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted, for his people Israel’s sake.
units.rightText: And David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had highly exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.

units.leftText: David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And David took more wives in Jerusalem and became the father of more sons and daughters.

units.leftText: These are the names of the children whom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
units.rightText: These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
rightNotes: 14:4 Shammua is a variant of Shimea; see 1 Chronicles 3:5|1CH 3:5*.

units.leftText: Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
units.rightText: Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,

units.leftText: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
units.rightText: Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

units.leftText: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
units.rightText: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
rightNotes: 14:7 Beeliada is a variant of Eliada; see 2 Samuel 5:16|2SA 5:16*.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went out against them.
units.rightText: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went in search of him; but David learned of this and went out to face them.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the valley of Rephaim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim.

units.leftText: David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?”
units.rightText: So David inquired of God, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hand?”

units.leftText: So they came up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal Perazim.
units.rightText: So David and his men went up to Baal-perazim, where he defeated the Philistines and said, “Like a bursting flood, God has burst out against my enemies by my hand.” So they called that place Baal-perazim.
leftNotes: 14:11 “Baal Perazim” means “The Lord who breaks out”.
rightNotes: 14:11 Baal-perazim means The Lord Bursts Out.

units.leftText: They left their gods there; and David gave a command, and they were burned with fire.
units.rightText: There the Philistines abandoned their gods, and David ordered that they be burned in the fire.

units.leftText: The Philistines made another raid in the valley.
units.rightText: Once again the Philistines raided the valley.

units.leftText: David inquired again of God; and God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.
units.rightText: So David again inquired of God, who answered him, “Do not march up after them, but circle around them and attack them in front of the balsam trees.
rightNotes: 14:14 Or aspen trees or poplar trees; also in verse 15

units.leftText: When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle; for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle, because this will mean that God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.”

units.leftText: David did as God commanded him; and they attacked the army of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.
units.rightText: So David did as God had commanded him, and they struck down the army of the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

units.leftText: The fame of David went out into all lands; and the LORD brought the fear of him on all nations.
units.rightText: And David’s fame went out into every land, and the LORD caused all nations to fear him.

units.leftText: David made himself houses in David’s city; and he prepared a place for God’s ark, and pitched a tent for it.
units.rightText: David constructed buildings for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.

units.leftText: Then David said, “No one ought to carry God’s ark but the Levites. For the LORD has chosen them to carry God’s ark, and to minister to him forever.”
units.rightText: Then David said, “No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God, because the LORD has chosen them to carry the ark of the LORD and to minister before Him forever.”

units.leftText: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up the LORD’s ark to its place, which he had prepared for it.
units.rightText: And David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.

units.leftText: David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
units.rightText: Then he gathered together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:

units.leftText: of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brothers one hundred twenty;
units.rightText: From the Kohathites, Uriel the chief and 120 of his relatives;

units.leftText: of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred twenty;
units.rightText: from the Merarites, Asaiah the chief and 220 of his relatives;

units.leftText: of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brothers one hundred thirty;
units.rightText: from the Gershomites, Joel the chief and 130 of his relatives;
rightNotes: 15:7 Gershomites is a variant of Gershonites; see 1 Chronicles 23:7|1CH 23:7*.

units.leftText: of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred;
units.rightText: from the Elizaphanites, Shemaiah the chief and 200 of his relatives;

units.leftText: of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brothers eighty;
units.rightText: from the Hebronites, Eliel the chief and 80 of his relatives;

units.leftText: of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brothers one hundred twelve.
units.rightText: and from the Uzzielites, Amminadab the chief and 112 of his relatives.

units.leftText: David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites: for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,
units.rightText: David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

units.leftText: and said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers’ households of the Levites. Sanctify yourselves, both you and your brothers, that you may bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, up to the place that I have prepared for it.
units.rightText: And he said to them, “You are the heads of the Levitical families. You and your relatives must consecrate yourselves so that you may bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.

units.leftText: For because you didn’t carry it at first, the LORD our God broke out in anger against us, because we didn’t seek him according to the ordinance.”
units.rightText: It was because you Levites were not with us the first time that the LORD our God burst forth in anger against us. For we did not consult Him about the proper order.”

units.leftText: So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: The children of the Levites bore God’s ark on their shoulders with its poles, as Moses commanded according to the LORD’s word.
units.rightText: And the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.

units.leftText: David spoke to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers with instruments of music, stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up their voices with joy.
units.rightText: David also told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their relatives as singers to lift up their voices with joy, accompanied by musical instruments— harps, lyres, and cymbals.

units.leftText: So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;
units.rightText: So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his brothers, Asaph son of Berechiah; from their brothers the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah;

units.leftText: and with them their brothers of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, the doorkeepers.
units.rightText: and with them their brothers next in rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-edom and Jeiel.
rightNotes: 15:18 Several Hebrew manuscripts and most LXX manuscripts (see also verse 20 and 1 Chronicles 16:5|1CH 16:5*); most Hebrew manuscripts Zechariah son of or Zechariah, Ben,
15:18 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah or Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Ozias

units.leftText: So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were given cymbals of bronze to sound aloud;
units.rightText: The musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals.

units.leftText: and Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with stringed instruments set to Alamoth;
units.rightText: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play the harps according to Alamoth.
rightNotes: 15:20 Aziel is a variant of Jaaziel; see verse 18.
15:20 Alamothis probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalm 46:1|PSA 46:1*.

units.leftText: and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre, to lead.
units.rightText: And Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead the music with lyres according to Sheminith.
rightNotes: 15:21 Sheminithis probably a musical term; here and in Psalm 6:1|PSA 6:1* and Psalm 12:1.

units.leftText: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the singing. He taught the singers, because he was skillful.
units.rightText: Chenaniah the head Levite was the director of the music because he was highly skilled.

units.leftText: Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.
units.rightText: Berechiah and Elkanah were to be guardians of the ark.
rightNotes: 15:23 Literally gatekeepers; also in verse 24

units.leftText: Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, blew the trumpets before God’s ark; and Obed-Edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.
units.rightText: Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer — the priests — were to blow the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah were also to be guardians of the ark.

units.leftText: So David, the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands went to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant up out of the house of Obed-Edom with joy.
units.rightText: So David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with rejoicing to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-edom.

units.leftText: When God helped the Levites who bore the ark of the LORD’s covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
units.rightText: And because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

units.leftText: David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bore the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David had an ephod of linen on him.
units.rightText: Now David was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark, as well as the singers and Chenaniah, the director of music for the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.

units.leftText: Thus all Israel brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant up with shouting, with sound of the cornet, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with stringed instruments and harps.
units.rightText: So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouting, with the sounding of rams’ horns and trumpets, and with cymbals and the music of harps and lyres.

units.leftText: As the ark of the LORD’s covenant came to David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David dancing and playing; and she despised him in her heart.
units.rightText: As the ark of the covenant of the LORD was entering the City of David, Saul’s daughter Michal looked down from a window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart.

units.leftText: They brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
units.rightText: So they brought the ark of God and placed it inside the tent that David had pitched for it. And they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

units.leftText: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the LORD’s name.
units.rightText: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.

units.leftText: He gave to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
units.rightText: Then he distributed to every man and woman of Israel a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.
rightNotes: 16:3 Or a portion of meat

units.leftText: He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the LORD’s ark, and to commemorate, to thank, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:
units.rightText: David appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to celebrate, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;
units.rightText: Asaph was the chief, Zechariah was second, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel. They were to play the harps and lyres, while Asaph sounded the cymbals

units.leftText: with Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
units.rightText: and the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew the trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.

units.leftText: Then on that day David first ordained giving of thanks to the LORD by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
units.rightText: On that day David first committed to Asaph and his associates this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:

units.leftText: Oh give thanks to the LORD.
units.rightText: “Give thanks to the LORD; call upon His name;

units.leftText: Sing to him.
units.rightText: Sing to Him, sing praises to Him;

units.leftText: Glory in his holy name.
units.rightText: Glory in His holy name;

units.leftText: Seek the LORD and his strength.
units.rightText: Seek out the LORD and His strength;

units.leftText: Remember his marvelous works that he has done,
units.rightText: Remember the wonders He has done,

units.leftText: you offspring of Israel his servant,
units.rightText: O offspring of His servant Israel,

units.leftText: He is the LORD our God.
units.rightText: He is the LORD our God;

units.leftText: Remember his covenant forever,
units.rightText: Remember His covenant forever,
rightNotes: 16:15 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts He remembers; see Psalm 105:8|PSA 105:8*.

units.leftText: the covenant which he made with Abraham,
units.rightText: the covenant He made with Abraham,

units.leftText: He confirmed it to Jacob for a statute,
units.rightText: He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree,

units.leftText: saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan,
units.rightText: ‘I will give you the land of Canaan

units.leftText: when you were but a few men in number,
units.rightText: When they were few in number,

units.leftText: They went about from nation to nation,
units.rightText: they wandered from nation to nation,

units.leftText: He allowed no man to do them wrong.
units.rightText: He let no man oppress them;

units.leftText: “Don’t touch my anointed ones!
units.rightText: ‘Do not touch My anointed ones!

units.leftText: Sing to the LORD, all the earth!
units.rightText: Sing to the LORD, all the earth.

units.leftText: Declare his glory among the nations,
units.rightText: Declare His glory among the nations,

units.leftText: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised.
units.rightText: For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised;

units.leftText: For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
units.rightText: For all the gods of the nations are idols,

units.leftText: Honor and majesty are before him.
units.rightText: Splendor and majesty are before Him;

units.leftText: Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples,
units.rightText: Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations,

units.leftText: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due to his name.
units.rightText: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name;

units.leftText: Tremble before him, all the earth.
units.rightText: tremble before Him, all the earth.

units.leftText: Let the heavens be glad,
units.rightText: Let the heavens be glad,

units.leftText: Let the sea roar, and its fullness!
units.rightText: Let the sea resound,

units.leftText: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD,
units.rightText: Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD,

units.leftText: Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good,
units.rightText: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good;

units.leftText: Say, “Save us, God of our salvation!
units.rightText: Then cry out: ‘Save us, O God of our salvation;

units.leftText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
units.rightText: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,

units.leftText: So he left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the LORD’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work required;
units.rightText: So David left Asaph and his associates there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to minister there regularly according to the daily requirements,

units.leftText: and Obed-Edom with their sixty-eight relatives; Obed-Edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;
units.rightText: along with Obed-edom and his sixty-eight relatives. Obed-edom son of Jeduthun, and also Hosah, were to be gatekeepers.

units.leftText: and Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests, before the LORD’s tabernacle in the high place that was at Gibeon,
units.rightText: And David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon

units.leftText: to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in the LORD’s law, which he commanded to Israel;
units.rightText: to regularly present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offerings, morning and evening, according to all that was written in the Law of the LORD, which He had commanded Israel to keep.

units.leftText: and with them Heman and Jeduthun and the rest who were chosen, who were mentioned by name, to give thanks to the LORD, because his loving kindness endures forever;
units.rightText: With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, for “His loving devotion endures forever.”

units.leftText: and with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God, and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
units.rightText: Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the music and instruments for the songs of God. And the sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
rightNotes: 16:42 Or instruments for the sacred music

units.leftText: All the people departed, each man to his house; and David returned to bless his house.
units.rightText: Then all the people departed for their homes, and David returned home to bless his household.

units.leftText: When David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Behold, I live in a cedar house, but the ark of the LORD’s covenant is in a tent.”
units.rightText: After David had settled into his palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the LORD is under a tent.”

units.leftText: Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart; for God is with you.”
units.rightText: And Nathan replied to David, “Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you.”

units.leftText: That same night, the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
units.rightText: But that night the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

units.leftText: “Go and tell David my servant, ‘The LORD says, “You shall not build me a house to dwell in;
units.rightText: “Go and tell My servant David that this is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build Me a house in which to dwell.

units.leftText: for I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought up Israel to this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tent to another.
units.rightText: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved from tent to tent and dwelling to dwelling.
rightNotes: 17:5 Out of Egyptis implied, but not included in the Hebrew; see 2 Samuel 7:6|2SA 7:6*.

units.leftText: In all places in which I have walked with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’
units.rightText: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
rightNotes: 17:6 Or judges; see verse 10.

units.leftText: “Now therefore, you shall tell my servant David, ‘The LORD of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel.
units.rightText: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.

units.leftText: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a name like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
units.rightText: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land.

units.leftText: I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not waste them any more, as at the first,
units.rightText: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning

units.leftText: and from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover I tell you that the LORD will build you a house.
units.rightText: and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies.

units.leftText: It will happen, when your days are fulfilled that you must go to be with your fathers, that I will set up your offspring after you, who will be of your sons; and I will establish his kingdom.
units.rightText: And when your days are fulfilled and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

units.leftText: He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
units.rightText: He will build a house for Me, and I will establish his throne forever.

units.leftText: I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not take my loving kindness away from him, as I took it from him who was before you;
units.rightText: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. And I will never remove My loving devotion from him as I removed it from your predecessor.

units.leftText: but I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom forever. His throne will be established forever.”’”
units.rightText: But I will set him over My house and My kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever.”

units.leftText: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
units.rightText: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire revelation.

units.leftText: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD; and he said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
units.rightText: Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?

units.leftText: This was a small thing in your eyes, O God, but you have spoken of your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have respected me according to the standard of a man of high degree, LORD God.
units.rightText: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O God, You have spoken about the future of the house of Your servant and have regarded me as a man of great distinction, O LORD God.
rightNotes: 17:17 Or and have shown me future generations

units.leftText: What can David say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your servant? For you know your servant.
units.rightText: What more can David say to You for honoring Your servant? For You know Your servant,

units.leftText: LORD, for your servant’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things.
units.rightText: O LORD. For the sake of Your servant and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and made known all these great promises.
rightNotes: 17:19 See 2 Samuel 7:20|2SA 7:20*; many translators 18*...For You know Your servant. 19*O LORD,

units.leftText: LORD, there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
units.rightText: O LORD, there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.

units.leftText: What one nation on the earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem to himself for a people, to make you a name by great and awesome things, in driving out nations from before your people whom you redeemed out of Egypt?
units.rightText: And who is like Your people Israel — the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself? You made a name for Yourself through great and awesome wonders by driving out nations from before Your people, whom You redeemed from Egypt.

units.leftText: For you made your people Israel your own people forever; and you, LORD, became their God.
units.rightText: For You have made Your people Israel Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.

units.leftText: Now, LORD, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, be established forever, and do as you have spoken.
units.rightText: And now, O LORD, let the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house be established forever. Do as You have promised,

units.leftText: Let your name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘The LORD of Armies is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel. The house of David your servant is established before you.’
units.rightText: so that Your name will be established and magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, is God over Israel.’ And may the house of Your servant David be established before You.

units.leftText: For you, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build him a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you.
units.rightText: For You, my God, have revealed to Your servant that You will build a house for him. Therefore Your servant has found the courage to pray before You.

units.leftText: Now, LORD, you are God, and have promised this good thing to your servant.
units.rightText: And now, O LORD, You are God! And You have promised this goodness to Your servant.

units.leftText: Now it has pleased you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, LORD, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”
units.rightText: So now You have been pleased to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever.”

units.leftText: After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.
units.rightText: Some time later, David defeated the Philistines, subdued them, and took Gath and its villages from the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: He defeated Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.
units.rightText: David also defeated the Moabites, and they became subject to David and brought him tribute.

units.leftText: David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
units.rightText: As far as Hamath, David also defeated King Hadadezer of Zobah, who had marched out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River.
rightNotes: 18:3 Hebrew his hand

units.leftText: David took from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them enough for one hundred chariots.
units.rightText: David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and he hamstrung all the horses except a hundred he kept for the chariots.

units.leftText: When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.
units.rightText: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of their men.

units.leftText: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David and brought tribute. The LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.
units.rightText: Then he placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.
rightNotes: 18:6 LXX and Vulgate (see also 2 Samuel 8:6|2SA 8:6* and Syriac); Hebrew does not include garrisons.
18:6 Or the LORD saved David; also in verse 13

units.leftText: David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And David took the gold shields that belonged to the officers of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took very much bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of bronze.
units.rightText: And from Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a large amount of bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and various bronze articles.
rightNotes: 18:8 Tibhath is a variant of Tebah; see 2 Samuel 8:8|2SA 8:8* LXX.

units.leftText: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
units.rightText: When King Tou of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
rightNotes: 18:9 Tou is a variant of Toi; also in verse 10; see 2 Samuel 8:9|2SA 8:9*.

units.leftText: he sent Hadoram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him (for Hadadezer had wars with Tou); and he had with him all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and bronze.
units.rightText: he sent his son Hadoram to greet King David and bless him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold and silver and bronze,
rightNotes: 18:10 Hadoram is a variant of Joram; see 2 Samuel 8:10|2SA 8:10*.

units.leftText: King David also dedicated these to the LORD, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
units.rightText: and King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had carried off from all these nations — from Edom and Moab, and from the Ammonites, Philistines, and Amalekites.

units.leftText: Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah struck eighteen thousand of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
units.rightText: Moreover, Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

units.leftText: He put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became servants to David. The LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.
units.rightText: He placed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites were subject to David. So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.

units.leftText: David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
units.rightText: Thus David reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people:

units.leftText: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
units.rightText: Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army;

units.leftText: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was scribe;
units.rightText: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests;
rightNotes: 18:16 Some Hebrew manuscripts, Vulgate, and Syriac (see also 2 Samuel 8:17|2SA 8:17*); most Hebrew manuscripts Abimelech

units.leftText: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.
units.rightText: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites;

units.leftText: After this, Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.
units.rightText: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son.

units.leftText: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.”
units.rightText: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.”

units.leftText: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”
units.rightText: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?”

units.leftText: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle at their buttocks, and sent them away.
units.rightText: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.

units.leftText: Then some people went and told David how the men were treated. He sent to meet them; for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”
units.rightText: When someone came and told David about his men, he sent messengers to meet them, since the men had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”

units.leftText: When the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.
units.rightText: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
leftNotes: 19:6 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds, so 1000 talents is about 30 metric tons
rightNotes: 19:6 1,000 talents is approximately 37.7 tons or 34.2 metric tons of silver.
19:6 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.

units.leftText: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and encamped near Medeba. The children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.
units.rightText: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba while the Ammonites were mustered from their cities and marched out for battle.

units.leftText: When David heard of it, he sent Joab with all the army of the mighty men.
units.rightText: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.

units.leftText: The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city; and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.
units.rightText: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country.

units.leftText: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose some of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.
units.rightText: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.

units.leftText: The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon.
units.rightText: And he placed the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.

units.leftText: He said, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you are to help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will help you.
units.rightText: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.

units.leftText: Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do that which seems good to him.”
units.rightText: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”

units.leftText: So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the front of the Syrians to the battle; and they fled before him.
units.rightText: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.

units.leftText: When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Joab’s brother Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel, they sent messengers and called out the Syrians who were beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the army of Hadadezer leading them.
units.rightText: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
rightNotes: 19:16 Hebrew the River
19:16 Shophach is a variant of Shobach; also in verse 18; see 2 Samuel 10:16|2SA 10:16*.

units.leftText: David was told that, so he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, came to them, and set the battle in array against them. So when David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought with him.
units.rightText: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, advanced toward the Arameans, and arrayed for battle against them. When David lined up to engage them in battle, they fought against him.

units.leftText: The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed of the Syrian men seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand footmen, and also killed Shophach the captain of the army.
units.rightText: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.

units.leftText: When the servants of Hadadezer saw that they were defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and served him. The Syrians would not help the children of Ammon any more.
units.rightText: When Hadadezer’s subjects saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore.

units.leftText: At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it.
units.rightText: In the spring, at the time when kings march out to war, Joab led out the army and ravaged the land of the Ammonites. He came to Rabbah and besieged it, but David remained in Jerusalem. And Joab attacked Rabbah and demolished it.
rightNotes: 20:1 Literally At the turn of the year

units.leftText: David took the crown of their king from off his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. It was set on David’s head, and he brought very much plunder out of the city.
units.rightText: Then David took the crown from the head of their king. It was found to weigh a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
leftNotes: 20:2 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces
rightNotes: 20:2 Or from the head of Milcom. Milcom, also called Molech, was god of the Ammonites; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.
20:2 A talent is approximately 75.4 pounds or 34.2 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: He brought out the people who were in it, and had them cut with saws, with iron picks, and with axes. David did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. And he did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
rightNotes: 20:3 Or cut them

units.leftText: After this, war arose at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they were subdued.
units.rightText: Some time later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were subdued.
rightNotes: 20:4 Sippai is a variant of Saph; see 2 Samuel 21:18|2SA 21:18*.
20:4 Or the giants; see also descendants of Rapha in verses 6 and 8.

units.leftText: Again there was war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
units.rightText: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines, and Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
rightNotes: 20:5 Or Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother; see 2 Samuel 21:19|2SA 21:19*.

units.leftText: There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot; and he also was born to the giant.
units.rightText: And there was also a battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot— twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,

units.leftText: When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea, David’s brother, killed him.
units.rightText: and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.

units.leftText: These were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
units.rightText: So these descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.

units.leftText: Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to take a census of Israel.
units.rightText: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.
rightNotes: 21:1 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary

units.leftText: David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know how many there are.”
units.rightText: So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, “Go and count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan and bring me a report, so that I may know their number.”

units.leftText: Joab said, “May the LORD make his people a hundred times as many as they are. But, my lord the king, aren’t they all my lord’s servants? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”
units.rightText: But Joab replied, “May the LORD multiply His troops a hundred times over. My lord the king, are they not all servants of my lord? Why does my lord want to do this? Why should he bring guilt on Israel?”

units.leftText: Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Therefore Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, then came to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Nevertheless , the king’s word prevailed against Joab. So Joab departed and traveled throughout Israel, and then he returned to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Joab gave the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.
units.rightText: And Joab reported to David the total number of the troops. In all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, including 470,000 in Judah.

units.leftText: But he didn’t count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.
units.rightText: But Joab did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count, because the king’s command was detestable to him.

units.leftText: God was displeased with this thing; therefore he struck Israel.
units.rightText: This command was also evil in the sight of God; so He struck Israel.

units.leftText: David said to God, “I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing. But now put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
units.rightText: Then David said to God, “I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing. Now I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”

units.leftText: The LORD spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,
units.rightText: And the LORD instructed Gad, David’s seer,

units.leftText: “Go and speak to David, saying, ‘The LORD says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.”’”
units.rightText: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”

units.leftText: So Gad came to David and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Take your choice:
units.rightText: So Gad went and said to David, “This is what the LORD says: ‘You must choose

units.leftText: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, and the LORD’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.’”
units.rightText: between three years of famine, three months of being swept away before your enemies and overtaken by their swords, or three days of the sword of the LORD— days of plague upon the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel.’ Now then, decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
rightNotes: 21:12 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate of fleeing; see 2 Samuel 24:13|2SA 24:13*.

units.leftText: David said to Gad, “I am in distress. Let me fall, I pray, into the LORD’s hand, for his mercies are very great. Don’t let me fall into man’s hand.”
units.rightText: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”

units.leftText: So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
units.rightText: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell dead.

units.leftText: God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he was about to destroy, the LORD saw, and he relented of the disaster, and said to the destroying angel, “It is enough. Now withdraw your hand.” the LORD’s angel was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
units.rightText: Then God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but as the angel was doing so, the LORD saw it and relented from the calamity, and He said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!”

units.leftText: David lifted up his eyes, and saw the LORD’s angel standing between earth and the sky, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem.
units.rightText: When David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem, David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.

units.leftText: David said to God, “Isn’t it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O LORD my God, be against me and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”
units.rightText: And David said to God, “Was it not I who gave the order to count the people? I am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, please let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house, but do not let this plague remain upon Your people.”
rightNotes: 21:17 Or I, the shepherd,see 2 Samuel 24:17|2SA 24:17* DSS and LXX.

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
units.rightText: Then the angel of the LORD ordered Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

units.leftText: David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spoke in the LORD’s name.
units.rightText: So David went up at the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.

units.leftText: Ornan turned back and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.
units.rightText: Now Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves.

units.leftText: As David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out of the threshing floor, and bowed himself to David with his face to the ground.
units.rightText: David came to Ornan, and when Ornan looked out and saw David, he left the threshing floor and bowed facedown before David.

units.leftText: Then David said to Ornan, “Sell me the place of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD on it. You shall sell it to me for the full price, that the plague may be stopped from afflicting the people.”
units.rightText: Then David said to Ornan, “Grant me the site of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to the LORD. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”

units.leftText: Ornan said to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes. Behold, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meal offering. I give it all.”
units.rightText: Ornan said to David, “Take it! May my lord the king do whatever seems good to him. Look, I will give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering— I will give it all.”

units.leftText: King David said to Ornan, “No, but I will most certainly buy it for the full price. For I will not take that which is yours for the LORD, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”
units.rightText: “No,” replied King David, “I insist on paying the full price, for I will not take for the LORD what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”

units.leftText: So David gave to Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place.
units.rightText: So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site.
leftNotes: 21:25 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.32 Troy ounces, so 600 shekels was about 6 kilograms or about 192 Troy ounces.
rightNotes: 21:25 600 shekels is approximately 15.1 pounds or 6.8 kilograms of gold.

units.leftText: David built an altar to the LORD there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the LORD; and he answered him from the sky by fire on the altar of burnt offering.
units.rightText: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.

units.leftText: Then the LORD commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath.
units.rightText: Then the LORD spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath.

units.leftText: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrificed there.
units.rightText: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifices there.

units.leftText: For the LORD’s tabernacle, which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, were at that time in the high place at Gibeon.
units.rightText: For the tabernacle of the LORD that Moses had made in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offering were presently at the high place in Gibeon,

units.leftText: But David couldn’t go before it to inquire of God, for he was afraid because of the sword of the LORD’s angel.
units.rightText: but David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

units.leftText: Then David said, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
units.rightText: Then David said, “Here shall be the house of the LORD God, as well as the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”

units.leftText: David gave orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house.
units.rightText: So David gave orders to gather the foreigners in the land of Israel, from whom he appointed stonecutters to prepare finished stones for building the house of God.

units.leftText: David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates and for the couplings, and bronze in abundance without weight,
units.rightText: David provided a large quantity of iron to make the nails for the doors of the gateways and for the fittings, together with more bronze than could be weighed

units.leftText: and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre brought cedar trees in abundance to David.
units.rightText: and more cedar logs than could be counted; for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a large quantity of cedar logs to David.

units.leftText: David said, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David prepared abundantly before his death.
units.rightText: And David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent — famous and glorious throughout all lands. Therefore I must make preparations for it.” So David made lavish preparations before his death.

units.leftText: Then he called for Solomon his son, and commanded him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Then David called for his son Solomon and instructed him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: David said to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of the LORD my God.
units.rightText: “My son,” said David to Solomon, “it was in my heart to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God,

units.leftText: But the LORD’s word came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly and have made great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.
units.rightText: but this word of the LORD came to me: ‘You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You are not to build a house for My Name because you have shed so much blood on the ground before Me.

units.leftText: Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.
units.rightText: But a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; for his name will be Solomon, and I will grant to Israel peace and quiet during his reign.
rightNotes: 22:9 Solomon sounds like and is probably derived from the Hebrew word for peace.

units.leftText: He shall build a house for my name; and he will be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
units.rightText: He is the one who will build a house for My Name. He will be My son, and I will be his Father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’

units.leftText: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you and prosper you, and build the house of the LORD your God, as he has spoken concerning you.
units.rightText: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, and may you succeed in building the house of the LORD your God, as He said you would.

units.leftText: May the LORD give you discretion and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Above all, may the LORD give you insight and understanding when He puts you in command over Israel, so that you may keep the Law of the LORD your God.

units.leftText: Then you will prosper, if you observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which the LORD gave Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid and don’t be dismayed.
units.rightText: Then you will succeed, if you carefully follow the statutes and ordinances that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.

units.leftText: Now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for the LORD’s house one hundred thousand talents of gold, one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone; and you may add to them.
units.rightText: Now behold, I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD— 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron too great to be weighed. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
leftNotes: 22:14 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces, so 100,000 talents is about 3 metric tons
rightNotes: 22:14 100,000 talents is approximately 3,770 tons or 3,420 metric tons of gold.
22:14 1,000,000 talents is approximately 37,700 tons or 34,200 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: There are also workmen with you in abundance—cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of work;
units.rightText: You also have many workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and men skilled in every kind of work —

units.leftText: of the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and may the LORD be with you.”
units.rightText: in gold and silver, bronze and iron— craftsmen beyond number. Now begin the work, and may the LORD be with you.”

units.leftText: David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
units.rightText: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:

units.leftText: “Isn’t the LORD your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people.
units.rightText: “Is not the LORD your God with you, and has He not granted you rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and His people.

units.leftText: Now set your heart and your soul to follow the LORD your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the LORD’s name.”
units.rightText: Now set your heart and soul to seek the LORD your God. Begin building the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the LORD.”

units.leftText: Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
units.rightText: When David was old and full of years, he installed his son Solomon as king over Israel.

units.leftText: He gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
units.rightText: Then he gathered all the leaders of Israel, as well as the priests and Levites.

units.leftText: The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
units.rightText: The Levites thirty years of age or older were counted, and the total number of men was 38,000.

units.leftText: David said, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the LORD’s house, six thousand were officers and judges,
units.rightText: “Of these,” said David, “24,000 are to oversee the work of the house of the LORD, 6,000 are to be officers and judges,
rightNotes: 23:4 Hebrew does not include said David,

units.leftText: four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised the LORD with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
units.rightText: 4,000 are to be gatekeepers, and 4,000 are to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise.”

units.leftText: David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
units.rightText: Then David divided the Levites into divisions according to the sons of Levi:

units.leftText: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
units.rightText: The Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
rightNotes: 23:7 Ladan is a variant of Libni; also in verses 8 and 9; see 1 Chronicles 6:17|1CH 6:17*.

units.leftText: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
units.rightText: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the first, Zetham, and Joel— three in all.
rightNotes: 23:8 Jehiel is a variant of Jehieli; see 1 Chronicles 26:21|1CH 26:21*.

units.leftText: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan.
units.rightText: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran— three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.

units.leftText: The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
units.rightText: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei— four in all.
rightNotes: 23:10 Shimei was possibly a son or grandson of the Shimei listed in verse 9.
23:10 Most Hebrew manuscripts; one Hebrew manuscript, LXX, and Vulgate (see also verse 11) Zizah
