units.leftText: Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah didn’t have many sons; therefore they became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
units.rightText: Jahath was the first and Zizah was the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family and received a single assignment.

units.leftText: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.
units.rightText: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel— four in all.

units.leftText: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to bless in his name forever.
units.rightText: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister before Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name forever.

units.leftText: But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
units.rightText: As for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.

units.leftText: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
units.rightText: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

units.leftText: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
units.rightText: The descendants of Gershom: Shebuel was the first.

units.leftText: The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
units.rightText: The descendants of Eliezer: Rehabiah was the first. Eliezer did not have any other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very numerous.

units.leftText: The son of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
units.rightText: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith was the first.

units.leftText: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
units.rightText: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.

units.leftText: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
units.rightText: The sons of Uzziel: Micah was the first and Isshiah the second.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
units.rightText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.

units.leftText: Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only; and their relatives, the sons of Kish, took them as wives.
units.rightText: Eleazar died without having any sons; he had only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.

units.leftText: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
units.rightText: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three in all.
rightNotes: 23:23 Jeremoth is a variant of Jerimoth; see 1 Chronicles 24:30|1CH 24:30*.

units.leftText: These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who were counted individually, in the number of names by their polls, who did the work for the service of the LORD’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
units.rightText: These were the descendants of Levi by their families— the heads of families, registered individually by name— those twenty years of age or older who worked in the service of the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: For David said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
units.rightText: For David had said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever.

units.leftText: Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”
units.rightText: So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service.”

units.leftText: For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were counted, from twenty years old and upward.
units.rightText: For according to the final instructions of David, the Levites twenty years of age or older were counted,

units.leftText: For their duty was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the LORD’s house—in the courts, in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house;
units.rightText: but their duty was to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD, being responsible for the courts and chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God,

units.leftText: for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
units.rightText: as well as for the rows of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size.

units.leftText: and to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise in the evening;
units.rightText: They were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening.

units.leftText: and to offer all burnt offerings to the LORD on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before the LORD;
units.rightText: Whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed feasts, they were to serve regularly before the LORD in the numbers prescribed for them.

units.leftText: and that they should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron their brothers for the service of the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place, and, under their brothers the descendants of Aaron, the service of the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
units.rightText: These were the divisions of the descendants of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

units.leftText: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
units.rightText: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father did, and they had no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.

units.leftText: David, with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their ordering in their service.
units.rightText: With the help of Eleazar’s descendant Zadok and Ithamar’s descendant Ahimelech, David divided them according to the offices of their service.

units.leftText: There were more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and they were divided like this: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses, eight.
units.rightText: Since more leaders were found among Eleazar’s descendants than those of Ithamar, they were divided accordingly. There were sixteen heads of families from the descendants of Eleazar and eight from the descendants of Ithamar.

units.leftText: Thus they were divided impartially by drawing lots; for there were princes of the sanctuary and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar.
units.rightText: Thus they were divided by lot, for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar’s and Ithamar’s descendants.

units.leftText: Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who was of the Levites, wrote them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar.
units.rightText: The scribe, Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite, recorded their names in the presence of the king and of the officers: Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of families of the priests and the Levites — one family being taken from Eleazar, and then one from Ithamar.

units.leftText: Now the first lot came out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
units.rightText: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib,

units.leftText: the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
units.rightText: the third to Harim,

units.leftText: the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
units.rightText: the fifth to Malchijah,

units.leftText: the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
units.rightText: the seventh to Hakkoz,

units.leftText: the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
units.rightText: the ninth to Jeshua,

units.leftText: the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
units.rightText: the eleventh to Eliashib,

units.leftText: the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
units.rightText: the thirteenth to Huppah,

units.leftText: the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
units.rightText: the fifteenth to Bilgah,

units.leftText: the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
units.rightText: the seventeenth to Hezir,

units.leftText: the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
units.rightText: the nineteenth to Pethahiah,

units.leftText: the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
units.rightText: the twenty-first to Jachin,

units.leftText: the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
units.rightText: the twenty-third to Delaiah,

units.leftText: This was their ordering in their service, to come into the LORD’s house according to the ordinance given to them by Aaron their father, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
units.rightText: This was their appointed order for service when they entered the house of the LORD, according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

units.leftText: Of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
units.rightText: Now these were the rest of the descendants of Levi:

units.leftText: Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
units.rightText: As for Rehabiah, from his sons: The first was Isshiah.
rightNotes: 24:21 Isshiah is a variant of Jeshaiah; see 1 Chronicles 26:25|1CH 26:25*.

units.leftText: Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
units.rightText: From the Izharites: Shelomoth;
rightNotes: 24:22 Shelomoth (twice in this verse) is a variant of Shelomith; see 1 Chronicles 23:18|1CH 23:18*.

units.leftText: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
units.rightText: From the sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
rightNotes: 24:23 Hebrew From the sons: Jeriah; see 1 Chronicles 23:19|1CH 23:19*.

units.leftText: The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
units.rightText: From the sons of Uzziel: Micah;

units.leftText: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
units.rightText: The brother of Micah: Isshiah;

units.leftText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno.
units.rightText: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.

units.leftText: The sons of Merari by Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
units.rightText: The descendants of Merari from Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.

units.leftText: Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
units.rightText: From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.

units.leftText: Of Kish, the son of Kish: Jerahmeel.
units.rightText: From Kish: Jerahmeel the son of Kish.

units.leftText: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after their fathers’ houses.
units.rightText: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
rightNotes: 24:30 Jerimoth is a variant of Jeremoth; see 1 Chronicles 23:23|1CH 23:23*.

units.leftText: These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites, the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.
units.rightText: As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites— the family heads and their younger brothers alike.

units.leftText: Moreover, David and the captains of the army set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals. The number of those who did the work according to their service was:
units.rightText: Additionally, David and the commanders of the army set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to prophesy with the accompaniment of lyres, harps, and cymbals. The following is the list of the men who performed this service:

units.leftText: of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. The sons of Asaph were under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied at the order of the king.
units.rightText: From the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. These sons of Asaph were under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied under the direction of the king.

units.leftText: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising the LORD with the harp.
units.rightText: From the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah , Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six in all — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
rightNotes: 25:3 One Hebrew manuscript and some LXX manuscripts (see also verse 17); most Hebrew manuscripts do not include Shimei.

units.leftText: Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
units.rightText: From the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
rightNotes: 25:4 Shebuel is a variant of Shubael; see verse 20.
25:4 Jerimoth is a variant of Jeremoth; see verse 22.

units.leftText: All these were the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
units.rightText: All these sons of Heman the king’s seer were given him through the promises of God to exalt him, for God had given Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

units.leftText: All these were under the hands of their father for song in the LORD’s house, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, for the service of God’s house: Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the order of the king.
units.rightText: All these were under the direction of their fathers for the music of the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God.

units.leftText: The number of them, with their brothers who were instructed in singing to the LORD, even all who were skillful, was two hundred eighty-eight.
units.rightText: Together with their relatives, who were all trained and skillful in the songs of the LORD, they numbered 288.

units.leftText: They cast lots for their offices, all alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.
units.rightText: They cast lots for their duties, young and old alike, teacher as well as pupil.

units.leftText: Now the first lot came out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons were twelve;
units.rightText: The first lot, which was for Asaph, fell to Joseph, his sons, and his brothers—12 in all;
rightNotes: 25:9 See LXX and the total in verse 7; Hebrew does not include his sons, and his brothers—12 in all;

units.leftText: the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the third to Zaccur, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the fourth to Izri, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
rightNotes: 25:11 Izri is a variant of Zeri; see verse 3.

units.leftText: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the seventh to Jesarelah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
rightNotes: 25:14 Jesarelah is a variant of Asarelah; see verse 2.

units.leftText: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the tenth to Shimei, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
rightNotes: 25:18 Azarel is a variant of Uzziel; see verse 4.

units.leftText: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;
rightNotes: 25:22 Jeremoth is a variant of Jerimoth; see verse 4.

units.leftText: for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
units.rightText: the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all;

units.leftText: for the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
units.rightText: and the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons, and his brothers— 12 in all.

units.leftText: For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
units.rightText: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers:

units.leftText: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
units.rightText: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,

units.leftText: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
units.rightText: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.

units.leftText: Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
units.rightText: And Obed-edom also had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,

units.leftText: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
units.rightText: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth. For God had blessed Obed-edom.

units.leftText: Sons were also born to Shemaiah his son, who ruled over the house of their father; for they were mighty men of valor.
units.rightText: Also to his son Shemaiah were born sons who ruled over their families because they were strong, capable men.

units.leftText: The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose relatives were valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
units.rightText: Shemaiah’s sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad; his brothers were Elihu and Semachiah, also capable men.

units.leftText: All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom with their sons and their brothers, able men in strength for the service: sixty-two of Obed-Edom.
units.rightText: All these were descendants of Obed-edom; they and their sons and brothers were capable men with strength to do the work— 62 in all from Obed-edom.

units.leftText: Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, eighteen valiant men.
units.rightText: Meshelemiah also had sons and brothers who were capable men— 18 in all.

units.leftText: Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him chief),
units.rightText: Hosah the Merarite also had sons: Shimri the first (although he was not the firstborn, his father had appointed him as the first),

units.leftText: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
units.rightText: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth. The sons and brothers of Hosah numbered 13 in all.

units.leftText: Of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like their brothers, to minister in the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: These divisions of the gatekeepers, through their chief men, had duties for ministering in the house of the LORD, just as their relatives did.

units.leftText: They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate.
units.rightText: They cast lots for each gate, according to their families, young and old alike.

units.leftText: The lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward.
units.rightText: The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah.
rightNotes: 26:14 Shelemiah is a variant of Meshelemiah; see verse 2.

units.leftText: To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
units.rightText: The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses to his sons.

units.leftText: To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
units.rightText: The lots for the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending highway fell to Shuppim and Hosah.
rightNotes: 26:16 Or on the upper road

units.leftText: Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
units.rightText: Each day there were six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two pairs at the storehouse.

units.leftText: For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
units.rightText: As for the court on the west, there were four at the highway and two at the court.
rightNotes: 26:18 Hebrew parbar; twice in this verse

units.leftText: These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
units.rightText: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and Merari.

units.leftText: Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
units.rightText: Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
rightNotes: 26:20 LXX; Hebrew As for the Levites, Ahijah was

units.leftText: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
units.rightText: From the descendants of Ladan, who were Gershonites through Ladan and heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite, were Jehieli,
rightNotes: 26:21 Ladan is a variant of Libni; see 1 Chronicles 6:17|1CH 6:17*.
26:21 Jehieli is a variant of Jehiel; also in verse 22; see 1 Chronicles 23:8|1CH 23:8*.

units.leftText: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: the sons of Jehieli, Zetham, and his brother Joel. They were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites:
units.rightText: From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:

units.leftText: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.
units.rightText: Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.

units.leftText: His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
units.rightText: His relatives through Eliezer included Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
rightNotes: 26:25 Jeshaiah is a variant of Isshiah; see 1 Chronicles 24:21|1CH 24:21*.

units.leftText: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
units.rightText: This Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries for the things dedicated by King David, by the heads of families who were the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the army commanders.

units.leftText: They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: All that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth and of his brothers.
units.rightText: Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, along with everything else that was dedicated, was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.

units.leftText: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
units.rightText: From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons had the outside duties as officers and judges over Israel.
rightNotes: 26:29 Or the duties outside (the temple) or the duties outside (Jerusalem)

units.leftText: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of the LORD and for the service of the king.
units.rightText: From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had charge of the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

units.leftText: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.
units.rightText: As for the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to the genealogies of his ancestors. In the fortieth year of David’s reign the records were searched, and strong, capable men were found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead.
rightNotes: 26:31 Jerijah is a variant of Jeriah; see 1 Chronicles 23:19|1CH 23:19*.

units.leftText: His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.
units.rightText: Among Jerijah’s relatives there were 2,700 capable men who were heads of families. King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.

units.leftText: Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in any matter of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: This is the list of the Israelites— the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions on rotating military duty each month throughout the year. There were 24,000 men in each division:

units.leftText: Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: He was of the children of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the army for the first month.
units.rightText: He was a descendant of Perez and chief of all the army commanders for the first month.

units.leftText: Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite and his division, and Mikloth the ruler; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: Dodai the Ahohite was in charge of the division for the second month, and Mikloth was the leader. There were 24,000 men in his division.
rightNotes: 27:4 Dodai is a variant of Dodo; see 2 Samuel 23:9|2SA 23:9*.

units.leftText: The third captain of the army for the third month was Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the chief priest. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The third army commander, as chief for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: This is that Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty. Of his division was Ammizabad his son.
units.rightText: This Benaiah was mighty among the Thirty and was over the Thirty, and his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.

units.leftText: The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The fourth, for the fourth month, was Joab’s brother Asahel, and his son Zebadiah was commander after him. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.
rightNotes: 27:8 Shamhuth is a variant of Shammoth or Shammah; see 1 Chronicles 11:27|1CH 11:27* and 2 Samuel 23:25.

units.leftText: The sixth captain for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The seventh captain for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The eighth captain for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The ninth captain for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjamite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The eleventh captain for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. There were 24,000 men in his division.

units.leftText: The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
units.rightText: The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. There were 24,000 men in his division.
rightNotes: 27:15 Heldai is a variant of Heled; see 1 Chronicles 11:30|1CH 11:30* and 2 Samuel 23:29.

units.leftText: Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
units.rightText: These officers were in charge of the tribes of Israel:

units.leftText: of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok;
units.rightText: over Levi was Hashabiah son of Kemuel;

units.leftText: of Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
units.rightText: over Judah was Elihu, one of David’s brothers;

units.leftText: of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
units.rightText: over Zebulun was Ishmaiah son of Obadiah;

units.leftText: of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
units.rightText: over the Ephraimites was Hoshea son of Azaziah;

units.leftText: of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
units.rightText: over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead was Iddo son of Zechariah;

units.leftText: of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the captains of the tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: and over Dan was Azarel son of Jeroham.

units.leftText: But David didn’t take the number of them from twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.
units.rightText: David did not count the men aged twenty or under, because the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky.

units.leftText: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and wrath came on Israel for this. The number wasn’t put into the account in the chronicles of King David.
units.rightText: Joab son of Zeruiah began to count the men but did not finish. For because of this census wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not entered in the Book of the Chronicles of King David.

units.leftText: Over the king’s treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel. Over the treasures in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah;
units.rightText: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the royal storehouses.

units.leftText: Over those who did the work of the field for tillage of the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub.
units.rightText: Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the workers in the fields who tilled the soil.

units.leftText: Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite. Over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
units.rightText: Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards.

units.leftText: Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowland was Baal Hanan the Gederite. Over the cellars of oil was Joash.
units.rightText: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the foothills.
rightNotes: 27:28 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite. Over the herds that were in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai.
units.rightText: Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds grazing in Sharon.

units.leftText: Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite. Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite.
units.rightText: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels.

units.leftText: All these were the rulers of the property which was King David’s.
units.rightText: Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks.

units.leftText: Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe. Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons.
units.rightText: David’s uncle Jonathan was a counselor; he was a man of insight and a scribe.

units.leftText: Ahithophel was the king’s counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
units.rightText: Ahithophel was the king’s counselor.

units.leftText: After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the captain of the king’s army.
units.rightText: Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah, then by Abiathar.

units.leftText: David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who served the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Now David summoned all the leaders of Israel to Jerusalem: the leaders of the tribes, the leaders of the divisions in the king’s service, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of all the property and cattle of the king and his sons, along with the court officials and mighty men— every mighty man of valor.

units.leftText: Then David the king stood up on his feet and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people! As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the LORD’s covenant, and for the footstool of our God; and I had prepared for the building.
units.rightText: Then King David rose to his feet and said, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people. It was in my heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and as a footstool for our God. I had made preparations to build it,

units.leftText: But God said to me, ‘You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.’
units.rightText: but God said to me, ‘You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war who has shed blood.’

units.leftText: However the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever. For he has chosen Judah to be prince; and in the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he took pleasure in me to make me king over all Israel.
units.rightText: Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of all my father’s house to be king over Israel forever. For He chose Judah as leader, and from the house of Judah He chose my father’s household, and from my father’s sons He was pleased to make me king over all Israel.

units.leftText: Of all my sons (for the LORD has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the LORD’s kingdom over Israel.
units.rightText: And of all my sons— for the LORD has given me many sons— He has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

units.leftText: He said to me, ‘Solomon, your son, shall build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
units.rightText: And He said to me, ‘Solomon your son is the one who will build My house and My courts, for I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father.

units.leftText: I will establish his kingdom forever if he continues to do my commandments and my ordinances, as it is today.’
units.rightText: I will establish his kingdom forever, if he resolutely carries out My commandments and ordinances, as is being done this day.’

units.leftText: Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the LORD’s assembly, and in the audience of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children after you forever.
units.rightText: So now in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your descendants forever.

units.leftText: You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for the LORD searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
units.rightText: As for you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him wholeheartedly and with a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands the intent of every thought. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever.

units.leftText: Take heed now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and do it.”
units.rightText: Consider now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and do it.”

units.leftText: Then David gave to Solomon his son the plans for the porch of the temple, for its houses, for its treasuries, for its upper rooms, for its inner rooms, for the place of the mercy seat;
units.rightText: Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the portico of the temple, its buildings, storehouses, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the room for the mercy seat.
rightNotes: 28:11 LXX; Hebrew does not include of the temple.
28:11 Or atonement cover

units.leftText: and the plans of all that he had by the Spirit, for the courts of the LORD’s house, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of God’s house, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
units.rightText: The plans contained everything David had in mind for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the house of God and of the dedicated things,
rightNotes: 28:12 Or had with him by the Spirit

units.leftText: also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of the LORD’s house, and for all the vessels of service in the LORD’s house—
units.rightText: for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of service in the house of the LORD, and for all the articles of service in the house of the LORD:

units.leftText: of gold by weight for the gold for all vessels of every kind of service, for all the vessels of silver by weight, for all vessels of every kind of service;
units.rightText: the weight of all the gold articles for every kind of service;

units.leftText: by weight also for the lamp stands of gold, and for its lamps, of gold, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps; and for the lamp stands of silver, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps, according to the use of every lamp stand;
units.rightText: the weight of the gold lampstands and their lamps, including the weight of each lampstand and its lamps;

units.leftText: and the gold by weight for the tables of show bread, for every table; and silver for the tables of silver;
units.rightText: the weight of gold for each table of showbread, and of silver for the silver tables;

units.leftText: and the forks, the basins, and the cups, of pure gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the silver bowls by weight for every bowl;
units.rightText: the weight of the pure gold for the forks, sprinkling bowls, and pitchers;

units.leftText: and for the altar of incense, refined gold by weight; and gold for the plans for the chariot, and the cherubim that spread out and cover the ark of the LORD’s covenant.
units.rightText: the weight of the refined gold for the altar of incense;

units.leftText: “All this”, David said, “I have been made to understand in writing from the LORD’s hand, even all the works of this pattern.”
units.rightText: “All this,” said David, “all the details of this plan, the LORD has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me.”

units.leftText: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the LORD’s house is finished.
units.rightText: David also said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will neither fail you nor forsake you before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.

units.leftText: Behold, there are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of God’s house. Every willing man who has skill for any kind of service shall be with you in all kinds of work. Also the captains and all the people will be entirely at your command.”
units.rightText: The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God, and every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work. The officials and all the people are fully at your command.”

units.leftText: David the king said to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is yet young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God.
units.rightText: Then King David said to the whole assembly, “My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced. The task is great because this palace is not for man, but for the LORD God.

units.leftText: Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood, also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.
units.rightText: Now with all my ability I have made provision for the house of my God — gold for the gold articles, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, and wood for the wood, as well as onyx for the settings, turquoise, stones of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and slabs of marble — all in abundance.

units.leftText: In addition, because I have set my affection on the house of my God, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:
units.rightText: Moreover, because of my delight in the house of my God, I now give for it my personal treasures of gold and silver, over and above all that I have provided for this holy temple:

units.leftText: even three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, with which to overlay the walls of the houses;
units.rightText: three thousand talents of gold (the gold of Ophir) and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the buildings,
leftNotes: 29:4 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces, so 3000 talents is about 90 metric tons
rightNotes: 29:4 3,000 talents is approximately 113 tons or 103 metric tons of gold.
29:4 7,000 talents is approximately 264 tons or 239.5 metric tons of silver.

units.leftText: of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all kinds of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to the LORD?”
units.rightText: for the gold work and the silver work, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who is willing to consecrate himself to the LORD today?”

units.leftText: Then the princes of the fathers’ households, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers over the king’s work, offered willingly;
units.rightText: Then the leaders of the families, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king’s work gave willingly.

units.leftText: and they gave for the service of God’s house of gold five thousand talents and ten thousand darics, of silver ten thousand talents, of bronze eighteen thousand talents, and of iron one hundred thousand talents.
units.rightText: Toward the service of God’s house they gave 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
leftNotes: 29:7 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds or 965 Troy ounces, so 5000 talents is about 150 metric tons
29:7 a daric was a gold coin issued by a Persian king, weighing about 8.4 grams or about 0.27 troy ounces each.
rightNotes: 29:7 5,000 talents is approximately 188.5 tons or 171 metric tons of gold.
29:7 Or 10,000 gold drachmas; that is, approximately 185.2 pounds or 84 kilograms of gold coins
29:7 10,000 talents is approximately 377 tons or 342 metric tons of silver.
29:7 18,000 talents is approximately 678.6 tons or 615.6 metric tons of bronze.
29:7 100,000 talents is approximately 3,770 tons or 3,420 metric tons of iron.

units.leftText: People with whom precious stones were found gave them to the treasure of the LORD’s house, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite.
units.rightText: Whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
rightNotes: 29:8 Jehiel is a variant of Jehieli; see 1 Chronicles 26:21|1CH 26:21*.

units.leftText: Then the people rejoiced, because they offered willingly, because with a perfect heart they offered willingly to the LORD; and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
units.rightText: And the people rejoiced at the willing response of their leaders, for they had given to the LORD freely and wholeheartedly. And King David also rejoiced greatly.

units.leftText: Therefore David blessed the LORD before all the assembly; and David said, “You are blessed, LORD, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever.
units.rightText: Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly and said:

units.leftText: Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.
units.rightText: Yours, O LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the splendor and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth belongs to You.

units.leftText: Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
units.rightText: Both riches and honor come from You, and You are the ruler over all. In Your hands are power and might to exalt and give strength to all.

units.leftText: Now therefore, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
units.rightText: Now therefore, our God, we give You thanks, and we praise Your glorious name.

units.leftText: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.
units.rightText: But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this? For everything comes from You, and from Your own hand we have given to You.

units.leftText: For we are strangers before you and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is no remaining.
units.rightText: For we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.

units.leftText: LORD our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.
units.rightText: O LORD our God, from Your hand comes all this abundance that we have provided to build You a house for Your holy Name, and all of it belongs to You.

units.leftText: I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.
units.rightText: I know, my God, that You test the heart and delight in uprightness. All these things I have given willingly and with an upright heart, and now I have seen Your people who are present here giving joyfully and willingly to You.

units.leftText: LORD, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you;
units.rightText: O LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire forever in the intentions of the hearts of Your people, and direct their hearts toward You.

units.leftText: and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”
units.rightText: And give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep and carry out all Your commandments, decrees, and statutes, and to build Your palace for which I have made provision.”

units.leftText: Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless the LORD your God!”
units.rightText: Then David said to the whole assembly, “Bless the LORD your God.”

units.leftText: They sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel,
units.rightText: The next day they offered sacrifices and presented burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with their drink offerings, and other sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

units.leftText: and ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness. They made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anointed him before the LORD to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.
units.rightText: That day they ate and drank with great joy in the presence of the LORD.

units.leftText: Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.
units.rightText: So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.

units.leftText: All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of King David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
units.rightText: All the officials and mighty men, as well as all of King David’s sons, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.

units.leftText: The LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
units.rightText: The LORD highly exalted Solomon in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him royal majesty such as had not been bestowed on any king in Israel before him.

units.leftText: Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
units.rightText: David son of Jesse was king over all Israel.

units.leftText: The time that he reigned over Israel was forty years; he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
units.rightText: He died at a ripe old age, full of years, riches, and honor, and his son Solomon reigned in his place.

units.leftText: Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
units.rightText: Now the acts of King David, from first to last, are indeed written in the Chronicles of Samuel the Seer, the Chronicles of Nathan the Prophet, and the Chronicles of Gad the Seer,

units.leftText: with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands.
units.rightText: together with all the details of his reign, his might, and the circumstances that came upon him and Israel and all the kingdoms of the lands.
